conversations.title: Small paws boarding in Lenoir Coty TN
conversations.text:
Last Thursday I drove 500 miles from my home to East Tennessee for my brothers celebration of life. I brought my 2 Pommies with me for company as this was my first trip to TN without my spouse who had passed away in the past year. 
I set up an account with rover.com and selected a place to board them for the weekend. But when I reached Lenoir City and looked for the place I couldn’t locate it nor could I get an answer on their phone. 2 gentlemen out for a walk tried to help me and came up with Small Paws as likely the place I was looking for.
So off I went with the directions listed in Google.  When o arrived i quickly realized this was not what I had booked. But when Nancy came out to greet me and the dogs, she was so welcoming and the boys seemed quite comfortable that I made the decision right there that they were going to stay at Small Paws until I returned home on Sunday. It was the best decision I could have made for all of us, even a convenient location to pick them up for the return home.
Awesome but go back 20 years there’s allot of photos still missing!!

conversations.title: Best way to store photos!
conversations.text:
I’ve always been a huge picture person. I love saving memories from special moments and and even everyday life. I’ve had pictures stored in hundreds of files on my computer for years. When I downloaded google photos it automatically took all of those and downloaded them to the cloud. After the download was completed, I received the option to delete all the old photos from my computer, which made my life a lot easier. You can easily find a picture of someone specific you’re looking for and share pictures back and fourth with others using personal links! This app has a ton of great features, if you play around with it you can find a bunch of cool stuff you’re able to do! The one downside is that if you are using your personal gmail, there’s only 15 GB of storage. I have used all of googles apps for as long as I can remember so my storage was way over the 15 mark. I recently purchased 100 GB for $1.99 which I will hopefully not need anymore after I go through all my data linked from my gmail. Another downside is the download quality of images and especially videos. I have it set to upload at original quality so there’s not much else I can do. Just realize if you’re shooting a high quality video shoot it might not actually be able to be downloaded at the same quality.

Overall this is the best way to save pictures. I’ve been a google photos user for about 8 years now and I couldn’t be more pleased with this app. I’m a huge supporter of google photos and have got many of my friends hooked on its benefits too!

conversations.title: Great app but lacking some features
conversations.text: I love this app. There's no doubt Google is doing the right thing when it comes to picture storage but there are some things lacking that I would like to be added. Having the ability to favorite pictures so you can have a folder for all your favorite pictures would be nice. We should also be able to change the layout inside albums instead of just the default view. I have albums that have almost the max amount of pictures in them and it's not the most pleasant experience to scroll through all those pictures in such a close-up view. I would also like to be able to put location information on individual pictures since many of my pics don't have location data on them. This is importance since most of the time I search up pictures by location and not being able to add location data is frustrating. Also opening Google maps to the location when clicking on the location on a picture should be a no brainer. Having a map of all the pictures you've taken around the world would also be a cool addition. Another thing I would love to be able to do is to manually tag faces in pictures. The app could potentially use this to better indicate which faces to find. Googles facial recognition is very good but not flawless and it's frustrating when it doesn't recognize a face and you can't manually tag the person in the picture. Another thing that would be amazing is if the app could recognize and tag people in videos. This would make me so happy since I have many many videos and it's hard to organize all of them.

conversations.title: Love it, but…
conversations.text: It was honestly too good to be true when they offered unlimited photo storage. Sadly that came to an end. When it was unlimited storage, I literally made it a point to bring up in conversation to every single one of my friends. Funny enough, nobody believed me when I explained how good it was, and they missed out if they didn’t download it. The longer you put off downloading this app, the more you will miss out on. This app was everything (and more) before any other game company was doing anything remotely similar. And I’m confident everything uploaded won’t be hacked or leaked. If you are a criminal or take photos of yourself commuting a crime, maybe don’t do that, but also I would suggest not using this service just in case. The government can subpoena your Google data and although I haven’t ever seen Google Photos being a turning point for a case, I don’t doubt that the government could make Google give them access to every single photo you’ve every taken. But that’s one end of the double edge sword - the other end is that every single photo you ever take will be automatically uploaded to the servers so you don’t have to do it yourself and so you never have to worry that any of your photos will ever be lost. But, now you have to pay for storage so that is on you for not using this app sooner. I use this app more than the photos app on iPhone.

So I can now share pictures without having to do so on fb! My husbands phone also syncs up with my account once I invited him and so his photo’s go with mine- which is neat to see!
It will also delete all the photo’s on your device that have been downloaded to google photo’s- saves tons of space (just got rid of over 2,000 pics on my device) and if I ever want that photo in my photo stream on my phone- I just click and save it to my phone. conversations.title: Great app, wrongly rated
conversations.text:
This app is one of the best as far as design and usability. It is also very useful, a blessing for people without much storage, and for sharing and making photo books.

Huge problem for me and my family, though: we use the Restrictions function for iPads and iPhones. We have removed browsers and limited web access to adult content and set the app install limit to apps rated 12+ or something like that. Google Photos is rated 4+ because Google told the App Store that they do not provide unrestricted web access. Well, they do. Unlike other apps, when you click the Privacy Policy link or something similar in this app’s settings, you get a page that can easily lead you to a google search page whose history is not kept. To get this search page, just keep clicking settings links on the webpages and trying to get to Google Account, from which you can find a link to google search. From there you can get to any website. And, it’s quite easy to come up with a search term that brings up porn in Images even with Apple’s setting turned on to Limit Adult Content.

I am writing this review as a shot in the dark, hoping Google will change it’s practice of putting those wide-open links in it’s Terms of Service and Privacy Policy webpages and other such places. Every single Google app can get you unrestricted web access, even though Google reports to the App Store rating system that web access is not available. If they at least reported accurately, the apps would be rated 17+ instead of 4+.

conversations.title: Google Photos' Biggest Problem
conversations.text: This app tries to work as a replacement for the default photos app, it automatically backs up photos, has an assistant to help make photos better, can recognize faces, has endless space. It has a lot of great features the default photos app doesn't have, and I have to applaud all the great things the app does. But it has a major problem stopping me from moving all my photos to Google Photos and sticking with it. There is no way to move albums you've made in the default photos app to a Google Photos album. This makes it terrible for someone like me with thousands of photos, with thousands already organized into seperate albums on my default photos app. It would take me hours to scroll through my entire camera roll on Google Photos to make my albums again. Even if you can't move entire albums from the default photos app to the Google photos app, you could make a compromise with an upload feature. Other apps, like Dropbox, let you upload photos by pulling up a menu that let's you see all your albums on your Photos app. That would be a start for letting people transfer their albums to this app instead of having to scroll through their entire library, sorting x from y. I would give this app a 5 star, but this problem is so detrimental, it ruins me using this app until this problem gets fixed. I hope this gets fixed later on, so I can use this app and free up the space I have on my phone later on, but until then this app is great but with a huge problem for completing moving from the photos app to this one.

My phone only has a storage of 65g and google photos only holds 15g. If you want more storage you have to pay for it. While I love the backing up and how it works and is easy to use. It needs to add more storage and I’m definitely not the only one who thinks that. conversations.title: Rich, vibrant colors and other fun touches
conversations.text:
I started using Google photos back when I had an LG and was still using XP on my desktop. Colors are richer, more vibrant. I like the feedback message I sometimes get on the bottom of select photos such as “Fix Lighting” or “Order Photo”.  It’s useful and the lighting adjust message is always spot on; makes the photo have more depth. The other aspect I like is when I find one of my photos had been “stylized” or “motion” had been added by whoever at Google makes these touches. I don’t mind the feedback and that’s what you get when you agree to allow them to modify. I took a hiatus from Google photos to work with another photo editing tool. When I returned, I found all my pictures neatly archived. Pleasant surprise when I found many I forgot I had. 
My only negative:  back when I was working with windows XP and an LG, Google photos had more filters and other features such as blemish blending and natural looking skin tone enhancers. The best was the awesome selection of frames to chose from. These features have been removed so I need to bridge my photos to another editing app for this. Other than that, Google photos is still my preferred primary editing tool. Thanks for the years of creativity and for thoughtfully archiving all of it.

conversations.title: Not foolproof - they lost my photos
conversations.text: I’ve been using Google Photos for years. I switched to Google Photos even though I use an iPhone and a Mac because my library was too big and it was taking up too much space on my iPhone.  if I deleted pictures from my iPhone, it would delete them from iCloud. So I needed a way to store my photos but still be able to delete them off my phone when I needed space so I switched to Google photos. Sometime last year I was looking for photos from 2013 and they’re almost all gone. There’s a few things left, but most everything is gone before 2017. I exchanged a multitude of emails with their support team and they couldn’t help me. I have a very large storage capacity and never missed any annual payments for that. I didn’t delete them. So there’s no reason that my photos/videos should’ve disappeared. Customer support was terrible. Just exchanging emails with them was disjointed and time consuming.  You can’t talk to anyone live so it’s a back and forth thing and they could give me any answers as to why they have gone missing. And then today I was trying to share some older photos but even though I can see them in the app when I try to share them it tells me that they need to be backed up first - but because the originals are not on my phone anymore the backup can’t happen. I’m crushed. These are all my kids photos from when they were babies. I thought Google would be the safest place to store them but clearly they’re not.

If I had to use one word to describe it I would use “sleek” just because everything runs so smoothly in sync together, plainly laid out; even not ever using it you can find all the stuff you need fast and easy. conversations.title: The more I use it, the more problems arise.
conversations.text:
While I like the ability to back up my photos and search on Google Photos (by person, date, or content), the more I use the app, the more problems I see. I’ve used this app for years but almost no overwhelming upgrades have been made in that time. Unless you count being able to identify pets, which GP thinks my brothers dog and a llama are the same animal. 
1. It’ll identify people for you so that you can search for pictures of your cousin John or something of the sort. Except that the algorithm that Google uses to identify people is woefully inadequate. If the picture is unclear, they’re wearing a mask, it’s only their profile, it’s a picture from behind, or for no reason at all, Google doesn’t identify them as people, thus you can’t tag that photo for your own purposes. 
2. Not all photos get moved. I have a picture of a friend and I feeding a baby animal at a zoo. It’s STILL on my phone but not anywhere on GP. And there doesn’t seem to be any way to upload it to GP manually. So, if I’d deleted that on my device to make room, I’d have lost it forever. 
3. There’s been a continuous problem for  YEARS about scrolling. Sometimes in the search feature, it only lets you scroll so far and then pops you back up to a different point. It’s been a problem that has been complained about but no fix has been forthcoming. 
Right now, it seems to be the best app for this photo storage with it's features. However, it is far from ideal and Google is such an innovative company that you have to assume that these issues aren’t being addressed on purpose.

conversations.title: No flexibility
conversations.text:
Google photos is an all or nothing app. Either it backs up all your photos, every single one, or none at all. Sometimes I use a screen shot as a quick reference for a few minutes then delete it from my phone, but then it’s still in the google account. It’s extremely frustrating to go back delete them from google, especially because that too is difficult to do. There’s no easy way to scroll through and delete quickly. You either have to view them from a small thumbnail and hope you’re not deleting something important or take a long time looking at each one and having to click multiple times to delete 1 photo. 
I am trying to free up space on my phone so deleting photos is supposed to be the easy choice since I have them backed up to google. However it either gives me option to delete ALL of the photos off my phone or none at all. There are still plenty of pictures I would like to keep sorted in the folders I created on my phone for quick reference. 
I’ve heard the argument “well they’re still on your phone you just have to open google photos instead of your regular photos.” This is of no use if you are somewhere with spotty or no internet connection. The app is not user friendly, the interface is not clean, and the way it sorts photos is of no real use to me. There should be extensive settings where I can toggle on and off different combinations of options.

conversations.title: Not good but has some qualities
conversations.text: don't get me wrong, the Google Photos itself is pretty good. Okay, the 15 GB offered by Google is honestly much better compared to other things like iCloud and Microsoft that only offer 10 GB for free, right? But the thing is, Google Photos is connected to Gmail and the other things, so whenever you run out of storage in Google Photos, that obligatorily blocks Gmail and all those other stuff. Deleting Google Photos and syncing is one of the most difficult things ever. Like I'm not bad at technology. I literally tried doing it with ChatGPT just to help me, and I couldn't do it anyways. Whenever I wanted to delete the photos because I didn't want to be synced because it would block my Gmail, Google Photos no matter what would not allow me If I stopped the permission from using my photos, then it would not allow me to look at my photos and not allow me to delete anything. Because I really did not need the storage. I just wanted to keep my photos safe so they wouldn't get deleted by accident. Which in return deleted it in Google Photos, and I had noticed that did they also delete my iCloud photos. And I lost 6,000 photos, 3 years of my Brazilian experience, and I have no photos of my home country. It's not accessible. Super hard to control if you don't give a lot of full permission. And I would not recommend unless you pay for it monthly.

conversations.title: Be careful what you upload and store!!
conversations.text: Although I love the unlimited storage and ease of album making, sharing, and management there are freaky unexplained things that happen to photos you know were in your collection but suddenly are no where to be found! I mean no where, not in the trash, archive, or backup places that you set any where. Case in point, I took a picture of the back and front of my business Credit card so that I could refer to my account numbers when I needed to while it was in the possession of an employee. I did so many times. When I looked for it today it had just vanished! I was not in the trash, archive, or back up places and I had not done anything with it since I last checked it. I don’t know if I was hacked, Google automatically removes such things, or maybe Google pulled for their own uses as per the Usage agreement we all sign without reading. That was not the first time something mysteriously disappeared from my photo collection yet is was the most vital. You will see that things tend to disappear for no reason and you will think you are going crazy and all Google will say is, “Check your archive, trash, and back up settings.” All these suggestions are no help when something totally disappears for no reason. BEWARE!!!

conversations.title: Secure backup for free
conversations.text: I love using google photos, and if you have the background app refresh on, it automatically keeps all your photos on the cloud. If not, just open it every few days or so and it will back them up when it’s open. It has helpful tips and touchups, but asks before making any changes (I almost always prefer the touchups to the original!) I take photos of lists and receipts, things I tend to only need for a few hours, and this app has a very helpful function that asks if I still need these types of photos and will gather them up for me to pick any to remove or keep. It also has an optional facial recognition feature - not for everyone, but I love it! It is easy to search for people and even pets! It may not be my most frequently used app, but it might just be my favorite. Today it asked if I’d like to clear space on my phone (yes, of course) and told me I had over 5k photos that had been backed up and were older, then with the press of a button sent them to my deleted folder in the photos app and told me how to permanently remove them from there. I’m upgrading my phone in a few days so that was super helpful, now the transfer will be quicker!

It’s great because it usually creates something that you’d like to have but you just never get around to making. Seeing old pictures of a trip with family and friends, the family pet doing something quirky, or being reminded of a special occasion can make your day. 

Candidly, I’m not a huge fan of the fact that Google has become this massive company with their hands in everything, but for utility apps like this there just aren’t many companies out there who have the time, money and imaginative software developers to create an app like this that actually makes it on to the App Store. For that reason I commend them. Now, if I could just figure out how to block every single move I make and web page I visit from them, I might just stop getting harassed by advertisements for things that I just searched for an hour ago on a completely different device connected to a completely different network!

conversations.title: Hate this stupid app
conversations.text: I’ve used google photos for 4 years now. Little did I know that this was a mistake! All of my photos have been backed up and saved to google photos over the years- and apparently this supposed storage app was actually a black hole. I am now out of storage space, and because of it, my phone practically doesn’t work anymore! It’s been the biggest mess! It’s keeping me from sending messages, receiving mail, taking photos, sending and receiving calls, and just generally using my phone! In an effort to fix this, I purchased a photo drive usb type thing to download all of my photos onto. Little did I realize that it only downloaded from a normal photos app, not google photos. So now I had my work cut out for me. I started off by trying to transfer all of my google photos pictures back to my normal photos app, and was very frustrated to find that the only way to do this was to go one at a time through every single photo. I gave up after about 200+ transfers. So I scoured the web searching for possible solutions. In the end I keep coming to the same conclusion. I either have to change all of my saved photos and videos to a lower resolution, or I have to pay money every month for more storage. I feel really stinking frustrated. I don’t know what to do. If anyone knows a solution I would really appreciate it, thanks!!!

conversations.title: Best thing for my cloud storage
conversations.text: I can’t image I can live without Google Photos for I moved all my photo storage to it. If it’s gone so are my photos! Not only it is free with unlimited space, but also it is so user friendly. I love the way an album is created, pics can be dragged into it or added anytime, before or after it's made. I love it's powerful search function and face recognition which can track same person all the way to his life time. I love it's in-app-photo-scanner which has so many uses.  I love it’s movie, animation, slides maker which give your ordinary pics a life instantly.I have so much fun playing around the app with my pics, video clips. It saves me so much money from not paying storage devices/services. It saves me so much time by using auto uploading and sync across devices. My photos are with me whenever I go. Uploading pics is super fast and reliable. Mostly it gives me a peace of mind knowing it’s here for safe storage needs which is priceless. I am so eternally grateful to have priceless gift among other things from Google. Thank you Google Photos for making the world better place for us people to remember!

conversations.title: Great app
conversations.text:
Google photos is terrific and they have certainly outdone Apple in the Photos app department. Sad that Apple can’t even make a better photos app than Google for their own devices. Google Photos has Apple Photos beaten in so many ways: 1) Google Photos shows camera info and even lets you edit the time of a photo. 2) Google Photos allows you to add descriptions to Photos. 3) Google Photos actually organizes your photos chronologically. Apple says they do in the Photos tab, but they don’t. They organize first by location than chronologically. It’s ugly. 4) Google Photos gives you a speed scroll up and down. 5) Google Photos allows for multi line album names. 6) Google Photos offers free photo storage (full resolution for Pixel owners) and (high resolution to everyone else). 7) Google Photos offers much nicer filters. 8) Google Photos has much better smart organization for their people, places and things Albums.

Google Photos is everything that Apple Photos isn’t. It still isn’t perfect, but at least it respects that people can think for themselves and offers many features that Apple Photos should, but doesn’t.

conversations.title: Amazing
conversations.text: I take a lot of pictures with my phone and with my SLR.  I have a large extended family and lots of grandkids.  I have 200,000 ++ digital photos dating back to my first digital camera in 2001.  I have digital scans of old 35mm slides. All this has been sitting on my hard drive doing no one any good.  I have uploaded each folder of photos on my hard drive onto GF.  Each folder on my PC has become an album on GF.  This resulted in the creation of hundreds of albums in GF.  Once in GF, I then share each album with the appropriate people for that particular album.  Google’s artificial intelligence (AI) is scary good.  The facial recognition is awesome.  It is able to recognize my brother at age 75 all the way down to age 8...automatically!  Below age 8 GF needs my help sometimes. So finding all the photos of uncle Harry is a snap.  Now all my kids have all the photos related to them on all their devices.  All searchable by person, date, location, setting (beach, mountains, etc).  They love it.  I love it.  All unlimited and free.  I still keep my SLR RAW files on my PC, but I have now made all my photos accessible to family and friends.  Simply amazing.

conversations.title: Invasion of privacy & deceiving to get you to buy storage
conversations.text: Google photos is using deception at its finest to get you to buy more storage. Worst user friendly app I have ever seen (how could google have such bad UX?) and you are definitely infringing upon my privacy rights. I didn’t realize backup was turned on when I downloaded the app so all the photos on my iPhone were uploaded on google photos and then I couldn’t use my google drive because storage was full!!!! I tried to delete the photos, which is also a tedious task, whatever happened to “select all” option???? But when I deleted it would delete the photos from my phone even when THE BACK UP AND SYNC WAS TURNED OFF. are you kidding me?? And then I tested to see if new photos i took on my phone would be uploaded when the backup was turned off, and it was, without any notification to alert the user! If anyone is having the same issue do this if you have an iphone: settings> scroll down to apps and click google photos> turn off “photos” to deny access to your photos by this app. And then to delete the ones that were already uploaded go to google photos on your laptop, select first photo while pressing down “shift” on your keyboard then scroll down to select last photo. This is how you select all and then you can delete.

conversations.title: I love it BUT ...
conversations.text: I absolutely love Google Photos! I haven’t had a problem with anything until recently. I’ve never used another cloud service except Google that I knew about until I discovered one day after my phone was stolen that was not the case. I got a newer Samsung phone a couple years ago and when setting the phone up I logged into everything from google, Samsung, Microsoft.. whatever.. anyways every now and then I’d get on my google account and back up whatever data created since the last time and I’m almost positive that meant contacts and photos as well. Well after my phone was stolen and I tried accessing some of the things I was looking for like photos and contacts and to my surprise NOTHING was there from the Samsung phone! Honestly, this is a little bit of my fault as well for a lack of knowledge.. i thankfully found the photos I was SOOO happy to have found in the one drive app. Not sure how my photos got sent to that cloud instead of google but it’s definitely something I’m aware of now and will pay attention to. Other than that little scare .. I’m grateful for this app.

conversations.title: Beyond brilliant
conversations.text: Google photos is probably the most useful app I have ever downloaded. Everything is easy and seamless. Being able to search people or animals by their faces is an amazing feature that I use often. I love that google photos creates albums, collages and movies on its own for me. Sharing photos is perfectly simple. I really like the archive feature, it’s relatively new. It allows you to put photos in a separate folder that you might not need such as screen shots or other photos you’d want to hide from your regular photos. Another feature I’ve been appreciative of lately is ‘rediscover this day,’ it allows you to see photos you took in this day during previous years.  I love this app. I tell all my friends and family to download it. Nothing else even comes close to what it can do. If anything I’d make a couple suggestions although I’m satisfied with the app without them. 1 - make a secret archive folder that can only be accessed with a password. 2 - allow users to create a custom collage (put the photos in the place they want rather than the app organizing them for you)

conversations.title: Ok for basic backup services but seriously lacking basic features
conversations.text:
Now I’ll be up front- it could definitely be me!  I haven’t met anyone who has a library the size of mine.  Things that should be simple are not- search for example.  It takes far too long to execute regardless if I’m using the phone app or on a computer.

Second- it is too tedious to tag people and pets.  If google only recognizes 3 out of 5 “faces” in a photo, good luck trying to get it to “see” the other 2.  It’s the same thing with pets.  If you accidentally associate a name with a person or a pet, it’s literally impossible to rectify.  

Now again, I don’t even KNOW how many photos and videos I have but I do know that I hit the limit for # of items in a folder.  I believe it stops counting at 20k.  To be fair I haven’t checked on that in a while; so perhaps they’ve fixed it.  Oh and one last silly annoyance- every time I access on my MacBook, it tells me to install the app because it’s soooo much better.  Literally says “get Google Photos on your computer”.  Story flaw- there IS NO APP for the MacBook!!!  When you click the link, you get the message “app only available for iPhone and iPad”.

conversations.title: Solid photo app
conversations.text:
I’ve been using google photos for over two years now and it has been an innovative, reliable way to backup photos and videos. The search feature is magic. There’s no other way to describe it. I searched for “headset” and a picture from five years ago popped up with me in the front seat of a small airplane with a headset on...it also somehow correctly recognizes people from birth to adulthood.  I don’t know about you, but I look nothing like I did when I was two years old. 

There are a couple improvements I would suggest though. First, editing photos could be significantly more robust. It currently has all the basic editing features you would find in most default phone photo apps. Second, a more clear, innovative organization method would be very handy. As it stands, I have tens (maybe hundreds) of thousands of photos all arrayed in a vertical flow with the months/years denoted along the side. Perhaps the option to automatically organize/rearrange into (gasp) folders by year, event type (wedding, vacation, etc) or person and other categories. Just a thought.

conversations.title: Great Over 50 App
conversations.text:
Generation X and Baby Boomers have some say in this World of Technology!  Typically we purchase the iPhone with less memory space available because let’s face it, “we’re not that techie”.  What we fail to realize we’re going through that stage of life with the plastic pull-out wallet photo album our grandmothers use to whip out on everyone, strangers on public transit included.  The only difference, our whip-out photo album is on our cell phones.  Suddenly you realize with all those photos and videos of the family, and your memory capacity notifications have you wishing you had bought the phone with more memory!  

THANK YOU GOOGLE PHOTO APP!  You have saved the day!  I can store my plastic photo flip-out album now on my Google Photos and have memory to spare!  The navigation on the app is so simple for all us “not so techie” 50+ people.  The document archive is a great feature too.  No more searching through photos for those paid bill screenshots.  I also love the photo editing suggestions, considering I’m not a professional photographer.
 This App is a must for all 50+!

conversations.title: Serves it purpose
conversations.text: I ran out of space in my iCloud and had to find something to back up my photos. I use Google for most everything else so it made sense to use it for photos. I like that you can access the photos, along with all the other Google products, while logged into my google account. It automatically uploads pictures I’ve taken onto my phone and when I need to free up space on my phone I can choose that option in google photos. It’ll send all of the pictures uploaded to the deleted file on my phone. There are a lot of photo products out there that have an option to upload photos directly from Google Photos like Shutterfly or even choosing pictures to have printed at your local Walgreens. The only complaint is that I wish it didn’t take so long to load the pictures and when you first click on the photos, it’s a bit pixelated so it takes a while to clear up. Although, it does hold a lot of pictures for free so I’d rather it continue to be free than those complaints be corrected and pay a fee for faster/more storage.

conversations.title: Almost Perfecf
conversations.text: I find the app so easy to use and share with others. It’s nice to have one convenient app to offload all my media to free up phone storage and a lot of the smart features like facial recognition and syncing them to my contacts makes sharing super easy. I love this app so much I transferred all my pictures into it, but I wish there was a way to mass edit multiple pictures’ date, time and location. You can edit them one by one but for example if you transferred in like 100 pics from a family vacation that took place in Hawaii about 3 years ago, then they are all automatically assigned as unknown date, time and location. It’d be super helpful to be able to edit all 100 pics to the same year and location in one go instead of one at a time. Other than that, new pictures taken from your phone automatically have the correct information entered, and it’s nice to see exactly where a picture was taken. Anyway, the app is almost perfect, but I’ll give it a 5/5 anyway since it comes so close.

conversations.title: Take me to that date
conversations.text:
Feature Request:

I’ve got years and years of photos uploaded with you.  When I search for a photo and you give me a result, I often want to review the rest of the photos taken from that date.  Currently to do so you have to back out and manually scroll through to the year, month and day or do another search for that month and year but then still scroll through to the moments to get around to the ‘time’ you’re looking for.  It seems weird that you cannot access the photos from a particular date from the already populated search results.  

I request that from the info of a photo that you’ve searched, that the date stamp be a hyperlink that takes you to the rest of the photos from that date.  Basically to your normal view/feed of your photos (such that you could scroll earlier or later if you wished) but by clicking the date you can go to all the photos taken at that time and not have to perform another search/operation to get there.

conversations.title: Couldn’t live without it
conversations.text:
Seriosuly Google Photos is a MUST for any sentimental human. I want to find a photo from something I did years ago? Can’t remember what year it even was? No problem. I can type in the location, or I can type in a key term like, “Renaissance faire” or “pizza” I don’t know, anything, and it’ll pull up related photos for me. I can usually find what I’m looking for quickly and I also discover some other forgotten gems in the process. 
I love that it has facial recognition, so I can easily narrow my searches down by people or pets. I also have albums for each of my kids that are automatically updated with photos containing their faces, without me having to do anything. I also automatically share these photos with family and friends. They get to see all of the kids photos/videos and all o have to do is take the picture. They automatically get backed up from my iPhone and automatically added to albums and automatically shared… I mean… how could I not use this?
Also, we recently discovered a new perk: partner sharing! My husband and I turned on partner sharing to share photos with each other so we no like get have to trade phones and airdrop yo each other haha.

Oh! And years ago I had Google photos back up my Facebook albums. Remember the mid 2000s when we would upload like 86 photos to a Facebook album? Well those are on Google now and I could delete them from Facebook. So yet another perk.

Anyway, clearly I highly recommend this. Been using it for years. No complaints.

conversations.title: Great Photo storage option
conversations.text:
I’ve only had this a day but so far it’s been great to work with.  Mostly thankful for the free (less than original quality) storage but there are some annoyances such as it won’t let you go into an album and select photos in that album to add to another album.  This would be great when you have 4,000 photos and have a 2016 Family album but you want to put all your favorites in a separate album as well as the main.  As it is currently you have to go into your 4,000 photos and look for the ones that you picked as favorites, which is hard as heck when you’re looking at thumbnails.  It’s hard enough that I plan to just re-upload all my favorites and see if I can make a 2016 favorites from that. 

To clarify, I’m talking about photos in your phone’s favorite folder.  They aren’t automatically made favorites on your Google Photos account.

The free part and the mass storage capability balance out this frustration to about 4 stars, because free mass storage when you have a 16GB iPhone that uses 4GB just for  iOS and doesn’t offer additional storage to be added, and requires 8 GB free in order to download and install the bi-monthly updates you can’t opt out of... well you can do the math.  It randomly has 7GB free so it auto-downloads the latest update, uses every single kilobyte so that when I go to take that amazing photo I suddenly see, the phone says no storage space available.  So I’ll never buy another iPhone again but until I get out of that storage nightmare this app is a lifesaver.  Maybe I’ll get a Google phone next.  We’ll see if usability of this app gets better in future updates. I usually love Google so hopefully this is just a glitch as it’s a recently introduced app.  I want more options than just “Remove from Album” for selected photos in an album.  Also being able to rotate selected photos all at ones would save hours.

conversations.title: Inconvenient and annoying
conversations.text: I don't usually write reviews but I HATE this app. I originally got it because it looked good, but I am just super annoyed now. I wanted to add the entirety of a specific album from my phone, and app the photos were really spread out so the only way I'd be able to find them is through the album, but when I went to add it there isn't an option to view already made albums from my default photo app, and you have to make a new album entirely from scratch without being able to view or select from old albums. How am I supposed to find anything?? I have so many photos. The only way I can actually find them when I need them is through my albums. After this I decided to delete the app, so I decided to delete all the photos off of it because I didn't want a bunch of random clutter if I decided to get the app in the future. I had already synced some of the photos because I assumed I would be keeping the app, but when I deleted them it deleted off my phone too, so I had to recover them. There isn't a way to delete them just off the app without removing it from your phone too. Why on earth did anyone think this app setup was good? Anyway, I am really annoyed with this. Such a let down tbh.

conversations.title: Doesn’t manually sync most of the time
conversations.text: I take all kinds of pics & don’t intend to keep them all, so I turned off the automatic sync feature. When I go to manually select photos to back up to a particular album I have created, 9 times out of 10, it will say it has backed up & when I go out of the app & back into it later to check on my new photo album full of pics, it won’t have any pics I put in the album. It also makes no difference if I’m trying to back up one photo or 300. The final variable is paying for the extra space, that doesn’t ensure you’re paying for better service. I have a paid & free account & Google Photos is equally abysmal at actually backing up my photos. If this problem isn’t resolved soon, I’ll cancel my membership & go to another more reliable service. Update to my review: in my paid subscription, I have not deleted & reinstalled this app at least 5 times in 2025 alone, & usually the whole albums feature isn’t available at all. Google, Apple, maybe both, are quite good at sitting on their laurels of what was once great service. As soon as I can find a service that shares photo albums, I will quit this app completely.

conversations.title: Does the work for me
conversations.text:
My family and I started using Google photos as a way for us to share all the pictures we capture when we’re together and soon realized it’s a great way to share photos from when we’re apart as well.  I love how easy it is to share photos and albums.  Works really well with my iPhone and allows me to keep my storage space on my phone freed up for more photos!
Another cool advantage to this photo sharing platform is the stylized photos and movies it randomly makes and suggests.  I only wish I knew how to make a stylized photo or action photo on my own.  
Google photos allows you to save and search by faces and places.  This includes even searching for your dog!  It’s a little scary how it makes a movie of “They grow up so fast” which is a compilation of photos of my baby from infancy to toddlerhood - how does it know it’s the same kid?  Incredible and freaky. 
In summary; I recommend Google photo to everyone that’s looking for an app to save and store photos.  It’s incredibly simple to use and does the work for you.

conversations.title: OMG!...I’m SO DONE WITH THIS APP 😱!,,

conversations.title: Photo storage as it should be
conversations.text: I love this app for a couple reasons. 1) the Auto Awesome recommendations made my the assistant are brilliant. They take what is otherwise an ordinary picture and enhance it to be something much more special. They give life to pictures. No other service does this and for free. 2) the search capabilities. I have 10s of thousands of pictures and searching through them could be a nightmare until now. Google Photos categorizes your photos based on location and the subject of the photograph itself. It's accuracy in being able to detect the subject is rather uncanny. I can now search my pictures far easier than before. 3) I know I said only 2 reasons but this one is important too. Free! You can upload your pics for free! Enough said. Some improvements I would like to see would be an option to delete the originals once they have been successfully backed up. NB: I do not work for or am in anyway affiliated with google. Just a regular consumer of its products.

conversations.title: Lost in Google Space
conversations.text: Ok, I’m not the most techy person. I know a little to usually mange or I find directions on how to do it, I do read it very slow (multiply times to myself then out loud and finally I ask my husband listen to this and tell me what I’m supposed to do and according to him his really smart in Google !! Please help, moved 8 years ago and they still have that address on file and is sending my Google photo books to a family that will be like why are getting this? Thank you KDT

conversations.title: All my photos get backed up
conversations.text:
It is awesome that I can backup every picture I've taken in the last 10 years worry free. Any pics I come across now I can just scan them and have a digital copy which over time will be a lot better than hard copies. I can also print pictures myself or have them done for a reasonable price on photo paper.
I had a friend who asked me to store almost 1000 pictures for her that have been taken over a period of 40 years. At the time we lived in the same town now we're 700 miles apart. I uploaded them to Google and made a folder for her and shared it so now she has access to them 24/7. She also uploads new pictures to the folder as she gets access to them so she'll haves digital backups. She was so very grateful that I did this because she forgot that she asked me to store them for her 6 years ago and told me that she thought she lost them forever. 
If you're considering Google photos I would strongly recommend that you do so that your memories can be shared for generations.

conversations.title: iPhone Users Problems
conversations.text: I absolutely LOVE this app. I have been using it for years, it has stored all of my important photos, and so much more. But let me just say this - Google Photos needs to find out a way to work in background on iPhone. You have to keep the app open for it to download your pictures, and as an iPhone user, I’ve noticed that it messes up my battery, having to keep the app open for hours and hours, at a time. So what I usually do is, I got to bed, open the app, and let it download over night. I usually buy a new iPhone every year or few months because of how bad it messes up my battery because of having to do this. Well, my worst experience was this morning. I woke up and my phone was extremely hot, like dangerously hot, and I was surprised that it didn’t catch the house on fire, thankfully. This was because I had Google Photos running all night (again, this is a brand new iPhone, because I have to buy them so often). Google Photos needs to find a way on iPhone to save photos in the background, instead of having to keep the app open and running for hours on end, and it messing up our batteries and phones. No other app does this to my phones, nor does it make me do that.

conversations.title: I can’t find anything I would change about it
conversations.text:
I think it happens to be flawless. I use it constantly easily three four times daily  .
      I’ve used it since picasa became google photos.   I don’t think about eating it because it’s smooth and flawless  I don’t even think about it. Only in thinking about a photo  organizer app. Did I consider how long it’s been on with me all the time that I remember it’s an app.  . I have an iPhone and I still won’t use any photo app but google photos  . 
    Freaking 15 gigs for feee storage for items I want kept at the highest possible resolution. And all other things I save sit for free not part of my limit . If it’s not a 4k movie with all close up intricate scenes then I never notice the quality difference between my not counting media and my storage counted media. 
 
          I challenge anyone to find a more functional user friendly massive storage space version of a photo manager app that is also free.   I have never found have that

conversations.title: Fantastic way to liberate your iPhone
conversations.text:
No room for the latest iOS update?  You probably are like a certain friend of mine who takes pictures of everything and texts pics of every meal she eats when traveling to new places. Your photos are great, but they are hiding out in text AND photo storage. Why do you need them in both places?  In fact, with this app you don’t need them on your phone at all!  If you are cool with Google knowing almost everything about you, which it probably already does, then have no fear!  This will solve your storage problem and make room for stuff you need on the phone. 

Set-up takes a while if you have multi-gigs of photos. Let it do its job and follow the Assistant’s guidance. Once done, install the latest iOS to see what you’ve been missing. 

One shortcoming I haven’t found an easy workaround for:  if you are already in a text or mail and want to send an older picture, it’s not easy to browse through your photo library in Google from within the mail app.

conversations.title: Lost photos/videos because the sync doesn’t work
conversations.text:
When my phone got stolen, I lost so many photos and videos that were on my google photos app on my iphone but weren’t on my google photos Web. I was missing photos and videos on the web version that spanned months, while my Google Photos app on my phone had everything to the most recent day. But I never recovered those pictures on Google Photos. Thank goodness for iCloud, otherwise I would’ve lost all of those pictures over the several months that Google Photos did not sync. 

Before my phone was stolen, Back up and sync were turned on prior. Backups were allowed over cellular data. So why did my photos from the past several months not sync automatically and quickly to google photos Web? Even now, they don’t sync until I log into Google photos web? Please fix so we don’t have to worry about losing memories when something happens to our phones. The syncing doesn’t always work and even now with my new phone I notice a huge lag in the syncing to the web version. The lag needs to be significantly reduced or eliminated because why should I pay for extra storage and it won’t actually sync anything?

conversations.title: Surprised how good yet not generally known by others
conversations.text:
This app pretty much does it all, as the best backup app I’ve found and it’s creative Assistant.  I’ve yet to run out of backup space and I have a ton of photos and videos. I don’t know how or why that works so well, but why pay for online backup space if you can use Google Photos? 
The Assistant suggests ready-made albums, makes movies, creates stylized copies of some of your beat shots, and even brings back memories from years past to see again.
About the only thing I don’t like is how fast it backs up your photos if you leave that feature turned on. So if you haven’t had time to delete some of the photos you don’t want to keep in your phone’s Photos folder, Google Photos will have already backed them up. Then it’s a little cumbersome to synchronize what you want to save. 
It also backs up your media on multiple devices, which is very handy because you can view all of those photos and videos in one place.
This is definitely a sleeper 5-Star app!

conversations.title: Great App
conversations.text: I just hope Google don’t hold my life in pictures as some kind of ransom, later on down the track. Google can be bought and sold right? Along with all my data. Putting faith in a company like this is a huge deal but they are not a country. They have no governing body that is connected to the people so... when you hand over your life in pictures, your facial details and all of your friends faces, places and times are essentially owned. There will be AI that will find patterns in people’s experiences gathered from this data that will be used to manipulate people in ways that we can’t imagine and probably won’t notice. And I know all this and yet the app makes it easier for me to enjoy the thousands of pictures that I’ve taken in my life. It uses algorithms to sort and make use out of all these captured moments. It’s really wonderful. So google you can have my pictures and data and the ability to manipulate me in some kind of emotional bliss, in exchange for this awesome service! Game-changer.

conversations.title: Fantastic
conversations.text: This is exactly what I have been looking for! The photos auto sync from my phone and across devices, as does every cloud photo storage service. But what I love about Google Photos is their facial recognition and sorting process. I wanted a system where I could select a specific person and see all their photos organized by year. Better yet, Google lets you filter by a specific person alone or the person with another or the person and a color or any other tag. It’s truly such a time saver. If I hadn’t found it, I planned to manually tag each photo — from 1960 to present day — with the person’s name. Also, you can share an album with anyone and have all photos featuring certain people to automatically add to the album. Unfortunately, the sort/filter options are not available for albums, so I ended up making a shared Google account so that everyone had the same convenience. I really hope they add that feature to albums

conversations.title: The. Worst. App. EVER.
conversations.text: I don't even know why I had this app in the first place, but I was recently notified by google that my storage was full and my Gmail would be shut down if I didn't clear more storage. I didn't want to buy more storage if I could clear some up first. The majority of my storage was being taken up by google photos which is weird because I don't use that app. I already have dropbox. So I decided I would delete all of the google photos to free up space for Gmail. WRONG. No warning, over 800 photos were not only deleted from google photos but from my actual iCloud Photos. ALL GONE. I was able to recover most of them (and had to pay to upgrade storage anyway. What a scam!) and got them back to my iCloud, but there are still some that are missing. This pisses me off beyond words. Nothing should be that easy to delete. No app should have that kind of access to delete photos permanently off of a device. There needs to be something in bold print before you delete pictures in google, warning you that the photos you're deleting will be erased from your iPhone photos app as well. Never using this app again. Will be telling EVERYONE I know how much I hate it. Thanks.

conversations.title: Great App for your Photos
conversations.text: This might be one of the most useful things on my phone. It reduces the space taken up by each photo while retaining the quality. It’s hard to complain about having more storage for other things. The only thing that I would personally love is a thing that scans through photos and shows ones that are duplicate images. I often scroll through a bunch of different art and enjoy saving them for references for my own drawings or just to admire, but occasionally I wonder if I have saved that image before. I also take some pictures that are the same or close to, and while the new grouping system is nice it doesn’t catch nearly everything I would like to get rid of. I also don’t have the ability to manually scroll through the several thousand images and remember each one that could be a duplicate image. All in all, it’s great and I wholeheartedly recommend it, just a suggestion for an improvement.

conversations.title: Impossible to use temporarily.
conversations.text:
Impossible to use temporarily. Do not download unless you want to pay for the rest of your life. At least make a secondary account so it doesn’t shut down your email if you do want to try it.  
Your service was terrible and extremely inconvenient. I only wanted to add a few pictures to share with someone, but that wasn’t an option. Then after I had shared them I wanted to end the service but guess what now my email won’t work. So I have to go in and delete thousands of photos one by one and it gets better. It also deleted them from my phone! How wonderful, now my email that I rely on for important communications involving finances mortgages etc. is at risk and all of my memories stored in my phone were also almost lost not to mention the endless frustration of trying to get the photo sharing to work the first week and then retrieving all of my photos. I had to create the shared album about 15 times or so before it worked. This service is absolutely terrible and and few small changes with the customer in mind instead of trying to make them pay every move nth for something they may or may not want could make it useful.

conversations.title: Best Photo App in existence.. Best of all it's free
conversations.text: Thee absolutely Very Best photo storage app to ever exist. The creators at Google continuously amaze me on how this app just keeps getting better. Since 2013 I’ve put all my trust into Google Photos to keep my photos safe & secure. We’re at the year 2020 and they’re still doing an amazing job. My photos are always readily available, in just a click of a button. I can access my photos from any device or computer. Saves me from having to run out of memory on my devices. I Never have to worry again about losing any more photos, if my Devices ever get lost, damaged or stolen. Best part of it all it's absolutely free. Thank You Google for all that you do!!!! Google I give you a 10 Star Rating. Now they charge a bit if you need additional photo storage.  Google Photos still provides free storage for the first gigs, not sure how many but it’s alot. I recently reached my quota but they charge Pennie’s to store my captured memories.

conversations.title: Truly the best
conversations.text: I’ve been a Google Photos user for years now, and whenever people complain of lost images and videos, running out of space, or losing their entire gallery because it was all stored locally on their phone I simply wonder why they don’t have this app. Just about should have this app; if you don’t have it, get it! It will be worthwhile. I rarely spend money on apps but I purchased the additional storage so I can store everything in full quality. Even if you don’t want to use up space with full quality, their high quality compression is just that, high quality. I love the features that allow me to search by person, and search by almost any keyword I want. This makes a long and laborious process do trying to find a specific photo from 4 years ago almost instantaneous. The bottom line is that Google Photos doesn’t just store your life’s memories, it lets you enjoy them over time in a meaningful, easy to access way.

conversations.title: Review update 2019, don’t get rid of this app
conversations.text: I don't know what I would do with out this app!  I have been using google photos for over 12 years. (That's on three children and 10+ bdays a year.)  In the beginning I uploaded my photos that I wanted to keep. So I did miss a lot of photos not uploading when I lost a phone, but ever since they started automatically uploading photos from my phone, if (when) my phone went bad, I didn't have to worry because my memories were already in google photos!  Even better, now that you can give google photos permission to delete already uploaded photos, my phone has tons of memory.  Plus my pics quality are good enough, I have been able to get some of my photos printed onto 16x20 canvases too.  I can say so much.  But I'll end with forget iCloud or Dropbox, why would you use anything else while Google offers Google Photos and so much more with goodie Drive?  Literally I love it, I depend on google way to much to help me keep storage of all my data.

conversations.title: Absolutely Essential!
conversations.text: Auto back-ups provide peace of mind, but that is just the beginning of why google photos is awesome. The ability to quickly organize photos into albums and seconds makes finding photos later easy. Sharing photos with friends is also amazingly fast. The auto assistant often makes great animations and videos from my photos, but I also have the ability to make my own custom animations and videos and the tools are intuitive and simple to use. Ability to find photos by searching for both thing and people is also quite impressive. My wife and I are also able to sync up our photos into a common space so that after any event pictures can be found organized by date and time. I also love that I have access to every photo I have ever taken because I have uploaded all the photos to Google Photos.  I recommend it to everyone I know because I love pictures and this is the best tool to Save, share, and edit quickly photos and videos.

conversations.title: So many issues
conversations.text:
I'm very frustrated with this app because I downloaded it to help me with the storage issues on my phone, but it's giving me separate issues of its own! The app says "backup complete" at the top of the page, but many of my pictures still have the white arrows going in circular motion. When I access google photos on the desktop, those items do not show up. I spent hours looking it up in forums and trying to fix it based on all the recommendations in forums, but nothing is helping. Only when I manually select the items and click "back up" do the arrows disappear, and it is irrational for me to sit there for hours selecting the items one by one when the app is supposed to do this automatically! On top of that, the app does not back up my videos. I really wanted this app to be worth it and to work for me and I'm very disappointed that it's not. Now I have to seek another solution and waste even more time worrying about this. At this point I'm not even sure if I should trust this app or continue using it, and I would not recommend it to friends with the issues I've been having! 
Save your energy and don't get this app!! 
-To Google: if I am contacted and the issues are fixed then I will change the review ..

conversations.title: A beautiful way to keep life in your pocket
conversations.text:
I have used this app for 5 years to backup all of my photos and videos. It does so automatically, straight from your library, without ever getting in your way. The app has saved nearly every picture and video I’ve taken in that time. 

It just so happens that 5 years ago is around the time I met my wife. 4 years ago is when my first child was born. This means that every picture or video of my wife and my kids, all of the firsts and lasts and everything in between, they’re all here. There are so many beautiful memories here that I can hold onto forever because of this app. 

I love scrolling through the years and months and just watching life’s story. The app is designed in a way that makes this easy and puts a strong emphasis on your media, rather than clutter. It even helps you clear clutter such as unimportant screenshots, document images, and even blurry or duplicate photos, so that you can focus on the special things. 

The Assistant that is built into the app makes everything so convenient. It has created so many amazing movies, collages, and animations for me (without me even prompting it to) that perfectly capture the little wonders of life. 

I don’t know what I would do if I didn’t have all of the things Google Photos has captured for me. Half of the time I didn’t even know it was doing it, but I’m so grateful that it did. If you’re not already using it, you should start now. You’ll thank me in 5 years.

conversations.title: Google Photos Lifer here 🙋🏻‍♀️
conversations.text:
I have been with Google Photos since the beginning I can literally scroll by year by favorites and find exactly what I’m always looking for. I love it when it surprises me with cute little videos of past events throughout the years. The fact that we can archive our photos digitally these days and no longer have to keep actual photos unless you want to print them. This is extremely useful when you decide to create a video montage of your best friend to commemorate her birthday. it’s amazing when you decide to go to a birthday party and show them a cute little video that you created with all of their past birthday parties. Not to mention when Google surprises you with a holiday video of all of your past events is truly amazing. 

Google Photos is the only place aside from, my phone storage that I keep all of my precious moments in one place. 

Thank you, Google and please continue making this app Great!

conversations.title: Really nice way to back up photos
conversations.text:
I really love how much space I can free up on my phone by saving my photos to google photos. My only issue is sorting my photos. I have so much on my camera roll even after going through and deleting some that I don’t want anymore, but it’s a pain to go through all my photos just to find one picture. I try to use albums to sort them out, but what’s disappointing is that when I put a picture into an album, it doesn’t disappear from my camera roll. It’s like I have a duplicate. I was hoping that the albums would be a good way of organizing my camera roll and hopefully making the general size of my camera roll smaller, but trying to find everything for the albums is really hard. 

Also, just a small suggestion. Some of my albums are huge and it would be nice if I could create subsections. For example, if I had an album labeled “vacation” then maybe I could have subsections like “day 1” “day 2” or “location 1” “location 2”

conversations.title: GREAT APP.
conversations.text: It’s a great app. Although, videos and photos should be made available offline for viewing. My Apple photos can do this but why not google photos. Love it. Love it a lot. For the app to categorize everything to Dogs, boats, people, places, food. I seriously love that. AND, I love that you can see which device the photo was made on. Super cool in my opinion and I love that feature a lot. Another feature I love is that really cool is that if can adjust and suggest you filter or adjustments needed to make your photo pop out more. But it’s just suggesting not actually doing it which is what I like. Overall the app is really great to have when I need to store some photos and able to share with people by simply adding them. Really cool app. 4 stars indeed. 1 star taken off. Sadly. Hope that feature comes soon!

conversations.title: I feel so safe
conversations.text:
I had the chance to unload 17k photos and videos off my phone. I am a digital hoarder.

When I was in elementary I had a house fire that burned almost all my toddler photos and baby photos in the early 2000s
When I discovered Snapchat I had that account for 6 years, had a relationship, had a bad break up, and my ex boyfriend stole my Snapchat account and deleted it just to destroy my precious held memories. (Junior high to highschool)
Afterwards I made another Snapchat account for a few years. Someone reported my account, to this day I don’t know what they reported, Snapchat deleted my account, with no way to recover anything.(19-22years old) 

Now as a 24 year old, I saved every photo, every video, I am terrified to lose memories again. It breaks my heart that I have nothing much to share of my past. 

I used iCloud before, when my old phone broke, and EVEN THEN, some of the files couldn’t transfer over. 

I found myself struggling with storage space for my phone, and iCloud didn’t seem to offer safe haven to hold onto my gallery. 

Google photos did, I dropped 17k of my precious memories, did a test run of deleting the original copy from my gallery, and finding the backup copy in google photos. It works! And to know I have 2 years to recover my thing’s before they’re gone? So reassuring! Now I have space on my phone to make more lifelong memories, I recommend Google Photos to everyone.

conversations.title: Amazing

Took old pictures with photoscan and send me back all of it. He send his album and now we have shared photoscan album. I'm over 70 year old and have old pictures colored and black and white. I did 3 kinds of edited pics. For comparison. I'm  very very amazed and delighted how google was able to do this. I'm very sure I'll be very proud to show this to all my friend in my forthcoming,
50th Wedding anniversary. Now l am looking for more antique picture to process nd it's keeping me busy. Thanks GOOGLE. AMAZING.

5 stars all the way. Improvements is continuous. Recently sending me reminders of things that happened a year ago.
I'll try to order Album for my Anniversary pictures.

conversations.title: Google photos is great

With apple my ICloud is being annoying and yelling at me for have like 1 dang photo but with google photos there’s soooooo much space too use so u can then delete the photos in your photos app and with google photos back up thing u can back up your photos to keep them and not have ICloud yelling at you. conversations.title: Love this app!
conversations.text: My phone was running out of space. I was constantly having to delete pictures so I could take new ones of my kids. Thankfully, my SIL told me about this app. I was able to transfer my 4,000+ pictures to the app in about 24 hrs. It took so long because I had so many to transfer at one time. I had to keep going in to check and manually transfer some here and there. But it was worth it. Once they were all successfully transferred, I was able to delete the pictures off my phone. The used space on my from when we 16 GB to barely 9 GB!! Now I don’t have to worry at all about how many pictures/videos I have or if I need to delete some to be able capture priceless moments of my kids growing up. I love the album storage and face recognition. It’s easy to search for people and places. I also love that it makes little videos for me to share. And that I can access all my phones from the app or my computer. I recommend this app to everyone!

conversations.title: Convenient but can be improved
conversations.text:
Like that it truly syncs while closed unlike Dropbox promises, and is much faster.

Areas that should be improved:

- Assistant can be improved but is convenient. Automatic trips don’t always work well and include random photos received around the same time, so the algorithm needs to be improved. Maybe consider both location and time. I travel a lot so it’s been easy for me to notice this.

- Sharing photos is easier and more intuitive on Dropbox, as it’s a URL to the actual photo, easy for anyone to open. With Google Photos it’s always weird for some reason.

- Would like much, much better filters without needing to remember Google search syntax (both would be nice).

- Would like to manage/create new people it doesn’t recognize (like my dog, sorry) and assign or tag them in photos, delete ones that don’t exist like celeb photos that get saved to camera roll automatically from WhatsApp. 🙄

- Also would be nice to edit or change locations for each photo it doesn’t grab.

- Albums can greatly be improved, but that’s another long review.

- Photo viewer should be improved, especially zoom.

I also love the visual map, dividers, and text feature for albums, they are great for road trips and just big/long trips in general. Ability to turn into photo books is cool too though I’ve never actually done it?

The ability to sync automatically without you even realizing or doing anything is where this app really excels, it’s even a bit creepy to an extent. 😂

conversations.title: Best memories in a movie!
conversations.text: I’m not one to write reviews...however this has been an amazing app which allows me to keep my valuable memories safe. I can store other items in my phone without losing videos or pics. I can change to a different phone or simply view to share with others, no matter where I am. It creates special albums and movies with the perfect title & music. It kindly reminds me about my “on this day” events..bringing me to tears at times. I can search by date or face recognition for specific memories. I simply love this app and am always recommending it to everyone. Absolutely free and absolutely great!!!!! Thank you so much google for touching my heart with all the amazing things you store and create for me. This morning I had a meltdown because of the movie you created “they grow up so fast”. Truly amazing...I literally cried...tears of joy. Being able to be transported to so many memories in such a short time it’s just the best feeling!!!!!! Thank you soooooooooo much again.

conversations.title: The Best

conversations.title: Solved my space issue
conversations.text:
Pictures probably take up the most space on our phones. But originally, our only other option is to download them to our computers every so often, or when we get the warning that our phone is almost out of space. But this app actually fixed that. 
-pictures I take on my phone are almost immediately uploaded to my Google photos account, so I can now completely delete from my phone any that I won’t need to get to right away. 
-space on Google photos is unlimited, and free! I’m guessing (I don’t know -just guessing) they’re selling them or something, because they only allow this deal if we upload full resolution pictures (nothing edited down in resolution). So don’t use this app if you take sensitive photos or anything you don’t want getting out to the public

Downsides (why only 4 stars)
1) I wish I could organize them into folders. Sure, we can categorize them by tag or category (I think Google also creates a description for them to search by — for instance, if I upload a picture of my dog, but don’t tag him as a dog, I can still find it if I search for dogs), bit it’s not like the folders I have on my computer. It’s just not as easy to organize them. 
2) sharing the pictures isn’t as easy as of they were on the phone. Instead, since they’re not actually on the phone, but on Google, I have to first download the picture to my phone, and only then can I share it. It would be nice if I could just do it through the app.

conversations.title: Be Careful if Using iCloud for Photos
conversations.text: I’ve been using Google photos for years and the app too. Everything was fine until the recent upgrade. Don’t believe Google Photos. While it says you can select which pictures it accesses on the iPhone, it won’t work unless you grant it “all access” to your photos. I do not want my phone pictures on Google; I simply want to access the app for pictures from my Nikon camera otherwise they are duplicates and taking up space for no reason and now Google want me to purchase additional storage. I also prefer iCloud for some things not Google. Sorry Google, some iPhone features are just better. There is no reason to have the option to limit access of phone photos and then have the app refuse to work if full access is not granted. This is ridiculous and a round about way of eliminating iCloud. I simply do not want Google Photos having this much control over my iPhone pictures. They are separate for good reason. You MUST give customers the ability to use the limited features on the phone. I don’t see why I cannot use Google Photos App simply to access my photos on Drive. It should be straightforward and VERY easy to give the right access without the all/nothing approach to using the app. Deleting pictures doesn’t work, not backing up STILL backups the phone screenshots and pictures immediately. I have now deleted the Google app waiting to see what to do next, but from the reviews; it seems this is a known problem. Google photos app was fine until you started trying to displace iCloud. Please be transparent as what you’re saying doesn’t match what your app is doing. Better yet - make it do what you say it’s supposed to do. It must be possible to use the standalone app on my iPhone without you accessing my iPhone pictures. I cannot ONLY have access to my Drive pictures only on the computer. I’m writing this review finally because I’m too frustrated the the Google photos app.

conversations.title: Way better than iCloud/iPhone Photo storage
conversations.text:
Many times it has happened to me that my iPhone has a problem and I go in to get it fixed, only to lose all of my data on my phone, my contacts and my photos. I have bought flash drives and downloaded my photos and videos onto them but I still manage to lose them because I am human and forget what I downloaded and when. I have tried printing all of them out, but some are videos and the cost is too much with the amount of pictures I take and try to print.
I have done a bit of research to find the best of the best for photo storage and this seems to be up there on the list. So, I have high hopes for Google Photos. I downloaded the app yesterday on my phone, set it up to automatically backup my iPhone photos and I am working on connecting it to my Mac! And so far, the experience has already eased my mind and I can't believe how easy it is to use. 
Thank god for google technology!!

conversations.title: My favorite app since 2011
conversations.text: I absolutely love this app. It’s user friendly, downloadable on any device, has a ton of storage, and is easy to set up because it’s connected to your Google account and settings. As a completely amateur photographer; I love to take pictures. They are memories, art, and a little look at what I am thankful for when I am down. It’s such a part of my life that I do t even see it as a hobby, more like a way I experience life. However, I’m very clumsy and loose or break my phone often. For years this meant losing my precious photos. But I’m 2011 I got this app; it took me another year to even realize it was saving my pictures from my phone. When I did I was so great full and happy. There were so many pictures I’d spent hours upset to have lost; all safe and able to be viewed and shared. Nowadays I make sure this is the first app that I download on any device that takes pictures.

conversations.title: Thousands of pictures gone
conversations.text: I had all of my photos in Google photos. A few months ago I decided to updated to a paid subscription. Sometime after June 14, the day of my dad’s funeral/memorial video. Thousands of my pictures disappeared. After a month google did not recover any of the missing pictures and will only refund one month, basically the month they have been giving me the run around on the lost photos. The did recover a few photos. Ones I actually deleted from a toxic job where I was a social media manager. So that was pretty triggering. They told me it was because I changed phones, even though I have changed phones multiple times in the past decade and accused me pf deleting the photos myself. I did not. Especially since the ones they recovered were actually photos I deleted. I am too emotionally exhausted to keep fighting with them. When I have the mental capacity I will move what little I have left to a private server. This is a warning save photos in multiple places and trust no one. My friend had the same issue with Dropbox. And after doing some searching, multiple people have had the same issue.

conversations.title: Running Photos list is a major organization downfall
conversations.text: Used to love this app but the biggest downfall is how you organize your photos. When you add a photo to an album it should get removed from your running photo list (not remain under photos). Follow the same format you have for the Google Drive app which allows you to organize your files into folders; once the file is in a folder it doesn’t show in your files list. Once you add a photo to an album it shouldn’t show in the photos list, making it easier to keep things organized and manage storage space better. When you have thousands of photos you're trying to organize and you have to scroll through all the photos you already put in an album to get the the photos you haven’t organized yet it’s too much.
