Please make this a feature to make organization easier and quicker.  I also miss receiving frequent Google created animations, collages, and movies created by google. I hardly ever receive them anymore, if at all.

conversations.title: Great photo storage app
conversations.text:
I absolutely love this app! I love that my husband and I can share our photo library to avoid having to always send photos to each other. I also love that I can use this as a FREE photo storage back up from my hard drive. It’s great peace of mind having a virtual hard drive that doesn’t require a monthly fee.

Recommended improvements: 
1. A duplicate photo search function - with our shared library it naturally duplicates a lot of images and it would be a huge time saver if google photos could recognize duplicates for review to delete 
2. A portrait orientation function that flipped sideways photos to the correct view. Having to edit each image can become time consuming. 
3. Ability to modify videos and collages.
4. The Face recognition technology has added to my library the zoomed in images of the people it’s recognizing. Which I had to then go in and delete those images. 
5. This is more for Apple than within google’s control. I use an iPhone and Mac and it would be so nice if when sending images or posting images I could select from my google photos library vs. my phones photo library alone. I have to go and screenshot or save the image from google photos to be able to use. - sidenote, some of the images don’t allow me to save to my photos, which requires me to screenshot them. Not sure why some photos allow me to save and some do not. Could be an Apple issue, but still a nuisance.  

Overall, I have great things to say about this app and recommend it to everyone I can!

conversations.title: The worst App experience ever
conversations.text:
I used to send my images between devices using Google Drive. It worked good for a few months until I always had problems about storage. I don’t know why, since my Drive was empty. It said ALL 15GB was used in Google Images, I don’t know why it would send them to this app especially without telling me. I usually delete a lot of images I don’t need anymore, but Google Images works differently. It automatically steals every image and video and saves it as-well, but whenever I delete an image from my device, it still exists in my Google Images. BUT this doesn’t work vice versa, meaning that whenever I delete an image from Google Images, IT ALSO deletes it from my main device. What was the thought process behind this??  
Along with this horrible abomination of an app, it’s terribly unreliable with saving some images. I’ve lost multiple important images at random times, I assume it’s due to low storage. But I can’t do anything about my storage unless I want to delete it from my device altogether, and it doesn’t even ask me before deleting them. 
Lastly, it’s buggy as hell this is awful.

conversations.title: I enjoy it but would love to have...
conversations.text:
I would like to see an option added where I can select photos I want to add to photo folder I’ve already created; and be able to search for the folder I want after hitting the plus sign...instead of having to scroll through them all to find the one I want. I have way to many folders to scroll and often miss the one I’m looking for. 

I know I can arrange them alphabetically or by last modified but they are not in either of those orders when your click the plus sign to add photos to a folder. It seems like they get put in order of recently accessed but I don’t always want those ones. A search option for the folder I want after selecting the photos I want to put in said folder would be helpful. Otherwise, I love google photos for due to space and ability to share pictures or whole albums with my family.  I was paying for additional space on apple because I have well over 100k pictures. I love pictures. 

Thanks!

conversations.title: Google backups
conversations.text: I lost 15 years that I can’t ever get back because I trusted google! My account got hacked and google refused to help me get my account back! I offered my ID, police reports, phone bills that showed my email address, everything I could think of! They would rather assist the hacker!!! I lost all my children’s photos, my dads voicemails  (and he’s deceased) not to mention my identity because they hacked all of my financial accounts and ruined my credit. Honestly, I could care less about my credit, I could minimize those losses, I cannot recreate my children’s lives or bring my dad back from the dead!!!  My entire Gdrive (income tax returns, credit card statements, notes, etc.)  all my google photos,  my emails, my contacts, my bank accounts, stock accounts, passwords, maps and map history... EVERYTHING!!!  Then I had my account set to notify a contact and allow them to download everything upon a certain time of inactivity. The day comes when the notice arrives and I am so grateful, but guess what... IMMEDIATELY, the account is accessed to prevent me from obtaining anything!!! BE MINDFUL of what you TRUST google with! You may support them; however, they DO NOT support you!

conversations.title: Don’t feel like paying Apple for more data?? Download this app
conversations.text:
Those 1080 and 4K videos and pictures were eating up my storage space on my phone and I didn’t want to pay $4.99 for more space. I had used the app on my previous phone but decided not to bring it forward to my iPhone 12 (insert buzzer sound). After while I was forced to delete unused apps and constantly archive photos. 

I really liked the apps option to store the photos at a lower quality and to archive older photos that aren’t being accessed or don’t contain any valuable content (ie., screenshots of YouTube/TikTok videos). 

My only gripe was the app did take a while to add my 2 years worth of photos. It will perform faster with the app open, but that means I’m unable to mindlessly use my phone for social media purposes. The option to auto-delete my photos after they were uploaded to the Google cloud almost made up for the length of time required to upload photos.

The facial recognition algorithm seems to be a tad better than Apple as Google doesn’t think my “so called” black children all look alike, like Siri does. I do feel it’s almost too good as it has started to auto-add new photos to my previously created photo albums. It did ask for my permission at one point (I think?). One recommendation I would offer is to add the option where Google asks periodically am I apply with the auto-populate options.

Happy space saving!

conversations.title: Surprisingly Hesitant With Change
conversations.text: I’ve never used Google Photos prior to this week, and now Verizon states I had to if I wanted to have easy access to all my devices photos once I activated my new phone and they weren’t just hanging out there in the, seemingly impossible to enter, iCloud storage. So far it’s been a refreshing change with and super easy to navigate thus far. The only thing I’ve come across as a flaw is, even though it states that the backup is complete and all photos have transferred successfully, sometimes when scrolling through my photos to choose one to view it will be crystal clear but when I click on it to view it solely it becomes extremely blurry. Why???? Besides that I only have 1 more thing that I find as a flaw, one that drives me crazy at that, and that’s the fact on some occasions it can take forever for some of my photos to pop up for viewing status!! I certainly don’t have time for that and in hopes that it fixes itself ASAP on that note!!

conversations.title: Amazing so versatile
conversations.text: This app is like a personal assistant itself. It can tell you which screenshots and picture are useless at this point so you can go and archive them or delete them. It edits pictures you already have with filters making them so much better, sometimes. If you run out of space on your phone or iCloud well then you can just go ahead put it here on google photos and it will have there ready for you no matter how much space it takes up. After backing it up on google photos you can just delete any photos you don’t want from your phone, and with the assistant feature that does all the editing it can also tell you which photos you can delete because they’re either gibberish, screenshots of something useless, outdated, or they’re practically the same picture as another one, it will tell you. All the picture that are backed up in the app are moved to your google drive so they’ll be same and accessible from any place you can get to google.

conversations.title: Great but room for improvement
conversations.text:
Enjoy the app but there’s def a few things that would make it so much better...

1.  If I could easily edit automatically generated animations.

Animations in my Opinion are the best part of the assistant feature.  However I hate when it contains one or two photos that I don't like or just aren't a good fit.  For example, it just made one and in half the pictures the person is in sunglasses and half without.  Now I know I could go in and make my own (but really who has the time) but ifi could just go into that animation and adjust it- well that would be so much better!

2. Your location service is pretty off.  Particularly when it puts together a movie it tells me everyone was done in the city I'm from- rather than where the photos were taken.  

3. A little concerned about quality of photos saved.  If I wanted to print them would they be a very high quality still? I've heard the app lowers the resolution.

4. Another animation comment. Annoyed that I couldn't easily edit from the generated animation I decided just once to try and search for those photos and recreate it.  However to select those photos for an animation I had to judge of of the thumb nail and ended up again including one I didn't want. At the very least it would be nice to be able to see the full photos BEFORE turning it into an animation.  But I'd still much prefer to manipulate an auto generated one.

But other than that- I really like it 😊

conversations.title: Not at all convenient
conversations.text: Honestly, google photos is one of their worst apps. It’s a great idea to have your photos in one space with your google account, however the execution of it was not great. First of all, it takes ALL of your storage on your google account. So if you don’t want to pay for extra space, you shouldn’t get it because it takes about 2 seconds for you to run out. Second of all, it is basically required (in order for the app the work) that you sync all of your photos from the device that you downloaded the app. This means that when you try to delete photos off the app (since you ran out of all your space and can’t get any emails) it will automatically delete off your phone which is literally the worst thing. Im saying this to everyone because I lost a lot of my important and meaningful photos since they do not mention this (at least not in a way that was very visible) which ends up sucking for anyone who innocently tries to clear up space. I hope google can make this app more convenient for everyone.

conversations.title: Hands down
conversations.text: Has made the most impact on my life compared to any other app I’ve ever used to date. I have had this app for I think close to either 12 or possibly 13 years now and I never imagined how much it would mean to me to be able to look back at my life like that. Constantly surprising myself with photos I forgot existed and randomly brings up memories with loved ones that I’ve lost & I couldn’t be more grateful and thankful to have been able to be reminded of them all no matter how much time has gone by. Probably even more so then before as the years have passed. Don’t hesitate to document your own experiences and history. You’ll regret having not started sooner. Hands down the most important and meaningful app I’ve ever used and consistently so for way longer than any other app I’ve ever downloaded. Thank you for protecting my personal photo journalism.

conversations.title: Display in latest update 👎🏻
conversations.text:
Why fix what ain’t broke? Don’t take away the original “day” photo clusters. 

I have enjoyed using Google Photos in the past, with certain updates adding helpful photo editing options (like “portrait” in Suggestions and magic eraser). I appreciate that my photos automatically populate in there and that edits save to my phone. All this is quite useful and intuitive. I don’t understand why they got rid of the daily view of photos, in which photos are grouped by day and then separated by a label and a blank space above the next day’s photo group below. Now everything is in a grid. Google claims that one of them is a “day” view, but all that means is that they’re still chronologically ordered. The tiles are just larger than in “month” view. There is no separation of days or months in any of the three modes. A little date “pill” appears near the top when scrolling, and that’s the only clue users have that they’re looking at photos from a different date. The visual cues are gone. Why take away a format that was working?!

conversations.title: Worse and worse
conversations.text: If I could give this app less than 1 star I could. Google Photos genuinely used to be one of the best photo storage and free photo editors available, but with every update they make good features somehow terrible. It's impossible to find anything anymore and the photo editing is split up into so many sections when it used to be neatly organized and accessable. The magic editor was great until they decided to change how to work it for whatever reason and now you have to get all of the thing you want removed in a photo all at once and if you make a mistake you can't just easily undo it, they make you start from the beginning. Even going back to edit previously edited photos will completely erase all the work you've put in before and make you start all over. I hate that they force all this AI editing onto you and make your pictures look even worse than before. I hate this app now and for the first time can say that Apple has a better photo app which is already bad on it's own. Go back to how this app was before the update and everything would be just fine

conversations.title: All around great app!
conversations.text:
I've been using Google photos for several years. I can't think of one complaint I'd have about it, so I'll give you some of my favorite features- maybe I'll remember something negative by the time I'm done lol. 

To start, don't turn off personalized suggestions! I love that there's no work involved with it, the app automatically stylizes, makes a collage, creates an album or adds 'color pop' (highlights something/someone & dowses the rest of the pic black & white). Maybe there's more suggestions, but those are what comes to mind at the moment. 

Can you say, 'free unlimited photo storage'?!? That alone is a major plus, having iPhone & not wanting to pay for storage, this helps tremendously! Google goes a step farther & reminds you to clear your clutter- whether that entails deleting the photos from your device or archiving 'junk' photos from the app (screenshots of text & whatnot), the app makes it easy! I love that there even is an archive, more free cloud space for my nonsense! 

Sharing is easy, moreso if you're a Gmail account holder I suppose but easy nonetheless. You can also add Google photos to iMessage apps to make sharing through there just as easy as sending through your iPhone photos. 

Huh, well I guess I was wrong- I can't think of anything I don't like about this app! I could probably go on about what I like but I think this is plenty long enough.

conversations.title: Intermediate users and above
conversations.text: Hi I’m Ryan and I’m happy that you have a app like this for me I really would love to have everything under one app that I would remember how To use it and have it work for me plus less password signing because now it’s like 5-6 google apps I have to have passwords for all other stuff like everything that it can do is just really awesome and I love it I just don’t like when I get lost and can’t find how to get back to it because I was looking for hours and lost it. Only other thing is I noticed that not all the time does it actually work and n to be having it reset exactly what it was like before I did anything like delete emails by cleaning up my phone space and I’ll ll at the app after about an hour and it’s all back to exactly what It was before deleting pictures and videos and emails each time the next time I even open the app it’s right back to the before I delete anything and stuff.  Sorry but thank you for your kindness to write me.

conversations.title: So-far, one word: #FANTASTIC
conversations.text: I had been using the Shoebox app for many many years for trusting them NOT to allow any third-party to have access to my images since it was encrypted (hope you do too #TEAMGOOGLE ). They are shutting down and would have lost EVERYTHING if I did not switch over to another app — did my research & downloaded the Google photo app yesterday. I’m currently in the process of switching over over 9000+ images to Google, as I literally type this on my mobile, and everything is going smoothly. Here’s to hoping that when all is said and done google photo will not disappoint me in the future, since they are a company that I trust you 100%. Highly RECOMMENDED for anybody that wants to free up space on the phone, laptops, desktops, tablets, etc. If you are using any other type of photo saving app, switch over to Google. #TEAMGOOGLE and keep being the technology revolutionaries that you are! (*PS: Google, please don't let me down 🙃)

conversations.title: Disappointed about several aspects
conversations.text:
Disappointed that the date for some photos, particularly old photos that I have scanned and subsequently updated the date using macOS photos, is not brought in as-is. It seems Google is relying on the EXIF dates rather than Apple’s metadata.

Secondly, when I rotate a live photo, it will remove the motion. That’s ok, I thought; I will rotate in Apple Photos which preserves the motion. The problem is that the motion of said photo now appears incorrectly in Google Photos. Apparently when you rotate a Live Photo with Apple Photos, google only sees the image as rotated, not the video. This seems like a bug actually.

The third aspect is that there is no way to scrub. I use the photo “bar” in Apple Photos to scrub quickly between different photos that are very similar. This allows me to detect which photo is the clearest, and to see other subtle differences. With Google Photos I can only swipe between photos. The animation that occurs when swiping causes me to lose context and I am unable to detect those subtle differences. Please add a scrub bar for fast scrolling with no animation like Apple Photos!

conversations.title: Impressive.
conversations.text: Wow. I’m genuinely surprised that such a massive company could make such a terrible non user friendly app. I was looking to backup my photos from my phone and trusted this app with my camera roll. I accidentally added all of my photos and videos and tried to delete some when I found it deleted from my camera roll too. I did some research to find out how to stop this when I realized I wouldn’t be able to receive any emails because my Google storage was full. I am in between jobs right now so this was a huge stressor and the possibility of my memories being gone from clearing space to get emails really added to it. When I figured out how to stop the app from deleting from my camera roll, I found I couldn’t delete all my pictures from Google photos in a simple manner. I researched the best way to do it and the deleting process took no less than 15 minutes. I had to just hope that my photos and videos wouldn’t be gone from my phone as I took all that time to delete and clear up storage. From what I can tell I don’t think I lost anything but why must it be so difficult.

conversations.title: Another baffling fail from Google
conversations.text: Another once-beloved and once relied-upon Google app being deleted from my phone after over a decade of use. It’s mind blowing, Google is going to be the first company in history to fail due to zero external factors or causes, just their own deliberate choices to absolutely cannibalize their own products. I just cannot understand why they would see people loving and relying on a product and think “let’s destroy every core aspect of this and make it into something that virtually everyone with a pulse absolutely despises”. It was one of the last apps that I still had some safety and security from the vile disgusting AI garbage slop, until today. They removed the “switch to classic search” option that was my last saving grace. I absolutely will not under any circumstances be engaging with their foul nauseating “Gemini” AI moronic waste of 1s and 0s. You really start to wonder if the people who work at this company are embarrassed for it to be known/embarrassed to associate themselves with such a bizarre downfall of a one-time innovative industry leader. Whole thing is sad and just reeks of greed, ignorance, and incompetence.

conversations.title: Garbage
conversations.text: As one other reviewer said, this app lacks the necessary flexibility to be at all useful. I have thousands of photos on my devices. I do not want or need every last one of them backed up in this app but it doesn’t give one the option to pick and choose. And where is it putting them? Who has access to them? Unknown. Also beware this app will take the place of your in-device photo albums— a photo deleted in the app is actually deleted from your device, not just within the app itself. This may be something that can be configured in settings but it isn’t at all clear when navigating the app initially. For something that is supposed to be for storage and organizing photos, I do not like how it so easily manipulates the photos in their original location on my device without asking me. So now a bunch of my photos that I would have preferred to keep only on this device are uploaded somewhere in the ether— can’t delete them in the app without actually deleting them from my device too. This is garbage. I’ve deleted it and will not be re-installing, and hopefully my photos are sequestered wherever they have ended up.

conversations.title: SO GREAT!
conversations.text: Aside from just the search engine, Google is a big part of my everyday/digital life; I use it for most everything. My family has Fiber internet and cable, I use Docs for school...the list goes on. And the Photos app is just another one of the things they’ve done right. The automatic backup is great, although at first I was hesitant to enable it because I thought it would take too long to get to all of my photos (however I was proven wrong—it works like a charm as long as you have high internet speeds). Not only does it do the main things you need it to do, but more! It has helpful features such as being able to make albums, the way it automatically identifies certain people/pets, and one of the coolest: Assistant. The assistant tab is so fun because it takes groups of pictures and videos and makes gifs, short movies compilations, and more. I could honestly go on and on. Everything is so great about this app!

conversations.title: Awesome and a LIFEsaver!!
conversations.text: Not only does this app work great and creates super cute collages, animations, and mini-movies all by itself (which you can save or delete), but it is the ONLY solution I found to the fact that iCloud/iTunes simply stopped uploading my photos/videos from my iPod 5 (or wouldn’t let me access or download them to my PC), and no other cloud service I tried (like MS’s OneDrive) could “see” that I had over 5,000 items to upload—except Google Photos!!! It was relatively fast and absolutely painless to upload every single one of them to Google Photos, however. (I did happen to upgrade my device to an iPhone 8, which is how I found out the app, so I never tried it from the iPod, but it would likely work, though might have been slower.) In any case, I wanted to post this in case anyone else is desperately looking for the same solution—and to thank Google for providing it, and making a really fun app, too!

conversations.title: Tremendous help to photographers
conversations.text:
I finally solved my photographic workflow process with Google photos. I have a huge library of raw images and finding a person, place or thing to retouch was a super hard problem to solve. I have over twenty years of images. Google photos to the rescue. I shoot in raw + jpeg and upload all the jpegs to google photos, keeping the original file name. My images are also archived offline. 

Then I am able to harness the intelligence of google to identify people, places, and animals. I can search on multiple criteria (such as color, location, etc) and quickly find shots. When I find the image in Google photos I can see the file name and then  can easily locate the correlating raw image in my offline archives to enable high resolution retouching. 

In addition, I carry virtually every shoot I have done on my pocket (on my phone). It is amazing! Thank you Google!

conversations.title: Duplicates are a pain; otherwise ✅
conversations.text:
Overall I love the Google Photo app. It’s made sharing pictures, both old and new, with my whole family so much easier. 
My biggest complaint is that there’s no easy way to remove duplicate photos that are automatically sent from my iPhone Photo app to the Google Photo app. Currently the user has to go through their entire library manually to find & delete duplicate items. 
There’s also some things I don’t want transferred to the Google app, but users are not given a chance to choose which photos are transferred to the Google Photo app; it’s done automatically. 
Two changes/corrections I would love to see include:

1. Some kind of program written into the app that would pull up all of the duplicate items in my account so I could have the option to delete them w/o having to go thru 3000+ photos manually to remove unwanted copies. 

2. An option to manually select the items in the iPhone Photo app that you want moved into your Google Photo app. OR at least give us a simple auto or manual option until something more detailed can be written.

I’m pretty sure if Google we’re to do a survey on those two items you’d find there’s a lot more subscribers than just myself who would like these ideas. I hope you actually see this feedback and find it helpful.

conversations.title: I’ve lost all of the progress on my wedding album twice… and several hours in the process
conversations.text: I tried to put together a wedding album for purchase using my iPhone and Google Photos this afternoon. After working for about an hour (and there is no way to save) The app crash losing all of my progress. Fine it happens. Then I tried to do the same thing using my tablet. I spent about two hours on at this time and was doing less touchups, hit the back button to go out of a page, and the back button freaked out and took me out of the entire album. Again there was no way whatsoever to save so I lost about three hours of my life and I feel like I am about to throw my tablet across the room. This is the most frustrating photo software I have ever used for this sole reason. It’s not that bad otherwise, but I don’t think that I will use Google again and I certainly don’t think that they will get the huge chunk of money that they were about to get for my wedding album. Additionally I will be trying to dissuade everybody I know from using Google photos for this purpose. Please add a freaking save option.

conversations.title: I love Google photos
conversations.text:
I’ve been a paying customer for years and tell others to use it. Only suggestion that comes to mind:

My family went on a trip recently. I created a shared photo album and we all added to it from our Google photos. The problem is that my own facial recognition definitions don’t work with their shared photos. I feel like they should still. There are like 1,300 photos and I want to be able to search them all for the few with all our family members included. When I do this, it only returns a couple that I took. I looked at my family’s shared photos for facial recognition but none of them show anything. Maybe this is a legal thing where you’re not allowed to but it just doesn’t make sense to me if they’ve already shared the photos with me and they are running through my facial recognition instead of theirs

conversations.title: Warning FREE  UP SPACE freezes
conversations.text: I am disappointed because the google photo app didn’t work as expected.  I chose google over icloud to backup all my pics and lost about 3k pics from Oct 2019 to today because the google Photos app kept freezing when about 3k photos were updated. I tried multiple times with no success so I deleted the pics from my phone directly since I already saw them uploaded in the photos app, I was just told by my rep that because of the sync function, my photos were deleted from the google photos app too. The free up space was not working. It worked to delete 50 or 200 or 150 pics at a time but froze to delete 3k+ pics. There must be a warning for people to avoid loosing their pics due to sync vs free up space not working and customers should be warned Not to Delete any pics from your phone as free up would freeze when trying to free up over 3k pics at a time. Bad combination. “Warning: Do not delete photos directly from your phone while sync is active even if you see the pics are in the photo app” because of the sync option, your pics will be deleted from the google photo app too. WARNING.

conversations.title: Super Annoying Bugs
conversations.text: First of all, I’m rating this one star because hopefully that will let it be seen. I really like google photos, heard about it from some family members and they love it. I just downloaded it, but when it uploaded my photos, I synced favorites thinking that it would put my favorites from my photos into google photos. WRONG. Instead, it favorited all of my photos, and now I have to search through all of my photos to find the old favorites again. Secondly, I have to keep readding photos into albums, because I will add them all to a google photos album and then they all are removed from the album for no reason (this has happened to all the albums I made just an hour ago). All in all, I really like google photos and how it has free storage and creates little memories for you, so please fix these bugs so I can enjoy it all the way!

conversations.title: One of the best apps in the App Store
conversations.text: When I went to Apple and they told me that I was going to completely lose all of my pictures and videos because of a "complete swipe" they had to do on my phone, I thought I was seriously screwed. Since I have a 2 year old, you know my phone is filled with tons of pics and videos. Once I downloaded this app with my existing Gmail email address, I was able to save every single picture and video with this app, and it only took about 30 minutes to backup around 800 images/videos. I also love that it automatically downloads all of my photos from my phone's photo album without me having to manually press a button for my pics to sync.. It's amazing, and I'm so glad I found it. Best part about it - it's free... and I believe I have unlimited storage for all of my pictures and videos that need to be backed up from my phone or my computer. Thanks Google! 😊

conversations.title: Love it.
conversations.text: Absolutely great app, organizes photos to YOUR preferences, not the phone or devices manufacturer. Tons of free storage with lost cost option to increase it substantially. Non intrusive, non invasive and puts you in control. Easy to use with lots of options on how you can organize your photos AND videos. Secure and stable with the power of Google backing it up. After about 300 pics my iPhone was constantly bugging me my storage was about full and kept pestering me to purchase additional storage from them, now that issue is a thing of the past, I backed everything up to the Google app and deleted everything from my phone, as stated there’s no issues with the app whatsoever, everything is as it should be and just as I left it from the previous access. I’m sold, it’s great. It even has basic photo editing. No issues or regrets whatsoever.

conversations.title: Beyond Expectations
conversations.text:
I got this because I was tired of my phone storage being full. The subscription plans are reasonable if you need the higher amount of memory capacities. Overall, a fantastic find. It creates memories and collages to look back on. It’s intuitive enough to review possible pictures that need to rotate as well as well as help review duplicates. It also will help delete photos that it uploads so you don’t need to worry about accidentally erasing pictures that are unsuccessful in uploading.

The few areas I’d say could use improvement is facial detection (sometimes when you label a person, it’s very good about grabbing those people; other times, it thinks two different people are the same person and the only way to unlink them from being identified/grouped as one person is to tediously go through each picture to identify they’re different. 

I also think screenshots and memes needs improvement since it does not detect many (or splits them up in odd ways).

And last but certainly not least, I hope there’s a way to upload pictures manually. Some of my pictures (especially older ones) have just never uploaded successfully. It simply finishes the backup but always misses these. As such, I’m stuck with about 500-1,000 pictures that are stuck to my phone and unable to upload into my cloud photos storage for whichever reason (I have not discovered the why yet but if I do, will update this review).

Overall though, super pleased with this app. My only regret is not having listened sooner when it was first suggested to me lol because it’s superb and I look forward to seeing how it continues to develop.

conversations.title: Well below Google’s standards
conversations.text: Google Drive is a wonderful product, proving the missing features in Google Photos is intentional.  Uploaded about 100 images as a test from my iPad.  Attempted to delete them...but Photos does not allow users to remove photos in bulk.  You must select each and every photo you want to delete.  This reeks of “we have your data and won’t let go.”  Took 700 photos on holiday?  Good luck managing that later. App also does seem to allow any means of direct album organization.  Organize by date automatically only.  Did 4 or 5 very different things that day? Nope, all one album.  You also may not select what photos sync and which do not (again, basic Google Drive functionality) so if you download images or graphics those are mixed in with your photos.  Want to remove a photo from the cloud that doesn’t belong with your photos?  Google will penalize you for daring by deleting it from your device automatically.  This “you will use the product in only the very, very narrow use-case we want you to” is what we expect of Apple, not Google.  Without user flexibility, not at all worth it, even for free.

conversations.title: Saves me so much time and space- favorite app.
conversations.text:
Google photos is my favorite app by far. I have photos on here that have been automatically downloaded to the app since 2012. It’s great because once they are downloaded to the app from my phone (which takes seconds) I can delete them off of my phone and save space! Google photos makes it so easy to look for pictures of my friends and it separated them by face and name- even my pets are separated. It also makes it easy to share them and text them to people on any format. Not to mention that it makes random movies and cool animation of photos you take which you can decide to keep or discard. It shows all the places that I’ve taken pictures around the world- there are so many features. 
Google photos is by far the best app on my phone. 
I’ve turned just about all of my friends and family on to the app and they all love it too!

conversations.title: The of essential apps to have on your phone.
conversations.text: This app is one of the greatest apps on phone especially if your looking at a smartphone that cost way too much for that high memory space you want. You can literally download this app and have every photo and video you ever owned on this app since it lives in the cloud. Before you even go crazy about the cloud not being secured, google has top notch security to ensure your photos and videos are safe. I’ve had google photo for the past 10 years and I can tell you from experience it has let me down. The backups are fast and simple as long as you have connection. Finding, sharing, organizing photos and videos are simple and easy. You just need a google account or gmail to get started. I love this app and will continue to always use this app. It truly is a great app. Oh did I mention you can access this app on everything? Well done google!

conversations.title: If you don’t have this app, what are you doing?
conversations.text:
I am just so thankful that this app exists!
How are they able to give us so much space? I take an obscene amount of photos and it’s truly a lifesaver. It’s easy to use and I like that it gives suggestions on how to clear the clutter and edit. The photo of the day feature is great for recalling fond memories...and for deleting those I’d rather forget. Its face recognition feature is really precise, which would be worrying if it weren’t so awesome. You can also do a keyword search and the results are pretty accurate. Album sharing/having collaborative albums is also great. I’ve yet to use the photo album ordering feature, but I’m glad it’s an option. 
The only thing is that I do wish they would switch back to the old layout, where the Assistant tab (instead of all my photos) is the homepage. It made more sense that way.
Overall, a must have app!

conversations.title: The best photo storage app
conversations.text: Google photos is the best and highest quality photo storage and photo organizer on the App Store. It automatically backs up your photos and stores them safely. I really love this app so much, thanks google for creating this, I also love This because you won’t need to worry about photo storage ever again because they’re safely stored in google photos. I have not had one backup problem and the app works as it should and flawlessly. I have backed up my photos and deleted all of them from apple photos and they’re still in google photos!!!!! 😁. No bugs, smooth experience, great search feature, a good set of features, and simple. The only thing I’d change is to make an in-app camera 📷. Otherwise this app is phenomenal and perfect. Thanks again google, forget apple photos with the icloud message “no more iCloud storage” because this app exists. Sorry cuz this review was a bit long.

conversations.title: Great app, missing a couple simple features
conversations.text: Has many options I really like, face recognition, ability to automatically add new photos to albums, great tools to make collages, photo books & movies, easy to share with others and collaborate. It’s lacking in some of the more simple options like the ability to order my albums the way I’d like, be able to sort alphabetically, or by date. I have multiple albums and I spend too much time scrolling through my albums when manually adding photos, and you can’t make an album within an album which would be another simple feature. For Example to make an album titled Christmas, and then be able to have separate albums within, for each year and there isn’t. It’s simply like making sub-folders within a folder like you can do with files and documents. The inability to do simple sorting & filing of my pictures is frustrating because I like so many other features in the app.

conversations.title: It’s my favorite photo app, but...
conversations.text:
I literally have EVERY SINGLE photo of mine sorted into an album. It makes things so easy to find and it’s wonderful. However, I have one major complaint: I can’t delete a photo from the album.
The only option I have is to “remove from album.”
So for example, maybe I have pictures that I took of my food over the years and I have a folder titled “food.” Well I can’t just delete all those useless food pics from the album page. Instead I have to scroll through THOUSANDS of photos in the photo page, hoping to come across my food pics. Or I have to click on the info button, figure out the date I took the picture, try to find that date and delete there from the photos page, and then repeat that for the hundreds of photos that are in that album. 
And that is one of example of the many ways this has inconvenienced me. So PLEASE I’m begging you, just add a “delete” option from the album menu. Please.

conversations.title: Love it
conversations.text: Works great and really does a lot of awesome things! I love all the extra features and tools such as magic eraser, and the face recognition, and photo editing features. I am a huge google fanatic. I think they really are one of the best tech companies out there. Google lense is one of the coolest things I’ve ever used with the reverse image search and whatnot. Also they offer a lot of really great services and products at a very good price compared to some other competitors. I’m a Google One member and I like that I can use all their features like VPN or extra backup storage and Google Photos even on an iPhone and all my other devices. They work great everywhere and my Google assistant is very smart…. lol probably much smarter than me. It never fails to impress me what they can do. I trust them with my life when it comes to all things future and technology. Huge fan here

conversations.title: My Google Photos App
conversations.text: I recommend this app to everyone that asks me about storage for their pics and videos. It saves me tons of space on my iPhone. I really like how you can file pictures under different people and then whatever picture you take with that person in it, it will go under their name and file. It also creates and makes suggestions showing you what your pictures look like on a canvas or in a photo book. They have a lot of options. Last but certainly not least my favorite part by far is the icon you hit when your on a picture with any kind of product you want to buy, it will bring up a list of places that sell that exact product. I use it for my sneaker addiction, when I can’t find a pair of sneakers I specifically am looking for this feature is my best friend. Hope you enjoy it as much as I do!

conversations.title: It can’t even view your iOS photo albums…
conversations.text: This app is missing a very basic feature. It does not support viewing the photo albums on your iPhone or iPad. It only shows your main Photo Library (by month) which contains all your photos and videos. This is very frustrating because I’m trying to upload some photos to a friend’s shared album (wedding). I already selected the ones I want to share and added them to my Favorites album. But I can’t even view my Favorites album in this app, or any other albums on my phone. Ironically, it lets you view the albums inside your Google Photos account. Just not the ones on your iOS devices. Conclusion: Unless you want to backup all your photos and videos to Google, or unless you want to sync all your favorites with your Google Photos favorites album, I do not recommend this app at all. I have iCloud backup already. I just want to share some photos with my friends but this app won’t let me do it. I don’t have time to go though the main library to figure out which are the ones I want to share and which ones I do not.

conversations.title: Please fix these things.
conversations.text: I love the app because it is easy to work with and has a lot of space to start with. It is not like I cloud where you have to go sign in to delete photos to have more space. You just go into the app and delete the photos you don’t want. I have just had a few issues with photos going where they need to. For example, I tried several time to put 1 screenshot in archive but every time I opened the app again it had not moved. I also keep getting annoying notifications that ask me to buy photo albums and print them. The app should ask if I want to do that once and then be done, not ask me every day. The one year ago and recent highlights folders the app makes on its own are pretty cool because you can see like oh I can’t believe that was a year ago. Overall, the app is pretty good if google photos could fix these things I would rate it a five star.

conversations.title: Love it =time saver
conversations.text:
Great app !!!! It pretty much does all the work for you but of course you make the final decisions. It cleans up your screenshots of papers and or receipts etc. and can put in a folder you made for them. It puts pics into to albums of what you’ve done that day like FB and you can either keep it or not up to you. does your friends phone book recognition and then you can either send the pics to them or not. Stuff you probably already do but now it’s something you don’t have to think about; the app is like a step a head of you and knows what you like while number one SAVES YOU SPACE AND AUTOMATICALLY RETRIEVES PHOTOS FROM PHONE AND DOWNLOAD AND DELETES them ONLY if you want to. The app will ask you if you want to free up space and then pics are
Gone from storage space on iPhone or iCloud can’t remember which one. So all and all it’s a great app and saves lots of space, time and money, money, money, money!!!!!!

conversations.title: Love it!!!
conversations.text: Google Photos is the best! It has helped me so much, especially since I take a lot of photos and videos, it helps me clear out some space, for new photos and videos. It also give my ipad more space for apps. I love how is makes, collages and animations, using similar photos. It also categorizes the different people, that have been seen on you photos, which helps, a lot on finding a specific photo, that you’d like to share with friends and family. Google photos, also customize the photos, I’ve taken, to make them look better, which makes my photos look AMAZING. I love how it backs-up all my things, without having to manually do it. Overall it’s the best app in my opinion, it makes my photography-addiction easier, simpler, and funner. Thank You Google. And anyone who took the time to read this. I hope everyone enjoys this app as much as I do, because to me, IT’S A LIFESAVER. 😍😍☺️☺️🤩🤗💜

conversations.title: Held my photos hostage
conversations.text: I downloaded this to use the reverse image search and all of the sudden it has uploaded all of my photos from my phone onto its cloud. That used up my 15 gb storage and I could no longer get emails. You’d think this would be an easy fix, but deleting the app and even deleting “Photos” from your Google account do mot fix this. They still keep your photos uploaded. The only way to do delete everything is to physically go through every single photo and delete each one. This took two hours of my life, but I had to do it because I needed my email. Felt like a hostage situation. Make sure you turn off all the syncing between the Google apps and your phone before doing this or else it deletes your photos right off your device as you delete them from the cloud. Insane way of doing things. What’s the point of the cloud— other than backup— if you have to keep all your photos on your phone too? I finally have everything sorted and my photos on my device seem to be safe. This whole ordeal made me so mad I wanted to just get rid of every Google account I have. Big middle finger to Google.

conversations.title: Love Google Photos
conversations.text: It’s simply #1 of all savers of precious moments in life that we capture thru the lens of our camera.! Whether it’s video or photos, Google captures and saves them all in the ever growing cloud basically forever! Now we can reflect on last week or last week ten years ago, all at the simple touch and swipe of your mobile device, laptop, or pc! Hands down the best app on the best web browser the internet has ever known. Google even likes to take your personal moments to create personalized home movies for all to enjoy randomly keeping you amazed with each and every update. If you don’t have Google Photos, you don’t have guaranteed security of your memories in which are priceless. Don’t waste another minute searching for the right app cause it’s right here in front of you because you never know what memory will expire to only be forgotten and lost forever. Kudos to you Google!

conversations.title: IF YOU DON’T HAVE THIS APP- GET IT
conversations.text: I found this app through my friend because I kept complaining about how annoying it is to sync crap on APPLE products. I needed something simple, something that worked quicker and was more user friendly. THEN my friend told me about this APP and I can’t believe I didn’t have it sooner. I’ve been using it for maybe 5 months now, and it’s the best thing that’s ever happened to me. It automatically syncs with your IPhone photo album and stores are the images for you. NO NEED TO BUY MORE STORAGE because there’s UNLIMITED storage!! After it syncs all your photos from your iPhone photo album, you can easily delete all those photos which continually saves you more room for more photos. Google photo app does it for you!! I also love the PEOPLE feature!! So you can easily find photos for a certain person because it identifies each individual. It’s great stuff!!!

conversations.title: Missing one thing I think
conversations.text: So I’ve been using Google Photos I don’t know for years and it’s great but the only thing is I think I have like 12,000 photos and or more and there’s no way except for going through manually for duplicate photos because every time they upload they have something different either the name or I edited it, but it’s essentially the same photo so if you could make a similar or duplicate photos setting that I could just hit and it would pull up everything that looks that would be awesome because it changes the name or something and if I do it later, it comes up later if that would be something you can work on that would be great just a suggestion thank you besides that I love having my photos on there so I don’t have to have them on my phone and that they pop up and show me things that happened like 13 years ago. 😀

conversations.title: My Google Photos experience
conversations.text: I love that no matter how many times I lose my phone, forget my password or have my identity stolen, I can trust that my photos are in good hands with Google Photos. As long as I use my settings to sync my photos to my account I’m Good. The only problem with that is that I’m always running out of storage and I’m having to upgrade my storage capacity. Then the fear sets in of Google holding my photos hostage until after pay my subscription. Luckily it’s dirt cheap to have lots of storage added to my account. I think I pay like $1.99 for 100gigs of storage. Don’t quote me on that but it’s somewhere in that vicinity. Needless to say after about 23 years of having my Google account I haven’t lost any pictures so I give them 4 stars. If I could merge all my accounts into one photo app then I’d give them 5. Thanks Google for being so dependable without me even noticing it till now.

conversations.title: Unlimited photo storage!!!
conversations.text:
I’m that guy that gets a 256gb iPhone just to manage all my photos. I have a lot going on majority of the time and am taking photos often. No memory goes uncaptured! 

So when I found out google photos allows you to backup your photos fairly seamlessly with the iPhone and have unlimited storage at that..... I figured there was some catch. I was wrong. It’s easy, it’s awesome. It works great. I also share albums with others, for example me and three others took a trip to the Dominican Republic. On the trip down I created an album in google photos and shared that album with them and we all flooded the album with all of our photos from the trip. It works great. Just be sure to note that unlimited storage comes with the one caveat that google is able to compress the photos first. I honestly don’t see a loss in quality, but others might.

conversations.title: Garbage App
conversations.text: Absolute trash. Great idea, executed like garbage. The number in the corner apparently refers to the photos not yet backed up, despite all those photos being shown in the app as if they have been backed up. Please make this more clear.  If I scroll through google photos and see 100 of my videos, I assume those videos are backed up and I delete them from my phone, freeing up 7gb and losing every video I took last summer.  User error for sure, but based on wretched, misleading information within this app. It's a great idea and I love it, but I hate it so much.  Please make the numbers more clear or make the un-backed up photos greyed out or have a danger sign on them or something if they're still going to be displayed in the app without being backed up.  As of now, Google Photos is a garbage app made by garbage people who I'm sure are brilliant and kind and well intentioned, but whose work unfortunately happens to be (almost amazing) garbage.  Goodbye Summer of 2017, now I have to rely on my sloppy memories like most of the rest of all people in human history instead of infrequently reviewing my shaky, unfocused, nostalgic videos. Ugh.

conversations.title: Love it...for the most part!
conversations.text:
I love that all of my images are backed up and I can access them anywhere. Makes me feel more secure because I love my photos! There are two areas that I have had trouble with which frustrate me. Sometimes it will be uploading images and it says it is done. Then when I go to make an album, it says it still needs to upload images and videos. This can be annoying!  Additionally, I created a shared album where others can contribute. One album my sister tried to add to and I never got the images and she tried more than once. Another time, my dad added images to an album, saw them and then a few weeks later they all disappeared but neither of us had done anything to delete them. One final thing I don't like is when I delete from Google Photos and it deletes from my device. I feel that should be independent.

The photo editor is good but I would like the red eye fix to be added like it was in Picassa.

conversations.title: Highly invasive requirements
conversations.text: I use Google Photos for work and family album sharing as a cross platform option for no. iPhone users. The issue I have is that there’s zero options to download photos and videos to google photos, then delete anything extra ONLY from google. You have to go to a computer, delete, and then reject the sync fix options. I’d like to sync to cloud photo and delete without allowing google to manage my iPhone photos. If you’ve ever had a hard drive or platform suddenly lose (or lock up with price hikes) your pictures, you’ll know that this is a bad option. If you use iCloud, it also deletes any photos, but their storage is 1/3 the price. Plus I only want to store my most prized photos and work stuff on Google. At this point I may have to just stop using it and switch back to free, and only have a few family pics. A simple option to delete only from google photos would fix this; but that coupled with those price hikes, I’m looking for better options and will stick with Dropbox for the big backups.

conversations.title: Deleted all my stored photos?
conversations.text:
I had been using Google Photos for a little over 4 years with no problem, making sure that all my pictures had been properly uploaded and stored in the app before ever deleting them from my phone itself, and it worked great. I had thousands upon thousands of images and videos saved within the app, and plenty of folders created to keep them organized. 
For some reason, some time around April or May, when I opened the app to go search for an old picture, ALL of my images were gone. The only ones remaining were the ones that were also actively on my phone’s camera roll. All my saved images were gone with absolutely no warning or explanation. I tried contacting the Google Photos “help” feature about it, as well as submitting a maintenance report, but I have never heard back. All my memories are gone with no explanation and no ability to recover them. I no longer trust the application and remain devastated that I ever did as it has left me without ability to access a large amount of cherished pictures.

conversations.title: Terrible UI changes (video vertical, hiding creations)
conversations.text:
Normally a great app, Google Photos took 2 steps backwards with the latest release. 
1. Nobody wants vertical/portrait video from Google Photos. It completely ruins the experience. It’s like Google spent years developing a beautiful airplane and then decides to chop its wings off because some competitors are flying helicopters instead. Terrible idea. Has nobody ever tried to watch a portrait mode video on a TV or computer screen? Even on my phone I take and watch videos in landscape because that’s the natural way human eyes work. Our eyes are arranged side by side on our face, not vertically. That’s why we have widescreens for watching videos, not tall screens... and there’s not even an option to choose landscape videos! You’ve given us no choice. Well stop using the feature. 
2. Complicated UI hides favorite features. I used to love scrolling though all of the new auto creations and suggestions in an easy to find location with good control. Now on the app, I can’t even find the creations - and they’re hidden in a clunky carousel with ‘highlight’ photos that I don’t care about - blatant copy of Facebook and instagram stories. I don’t use FB or Instagram partly because I don’t like being forced into a carousel with limited ability to select what I view or navigate the stories (tapping vs swiping, no rewinding videos etc.). I want precision, visibility, and for the user to be in control of the experience. Google has taken that away in an effort to be more like the competition. This completely misses the point. I choose Google because it’s differentiated and a better experience, for varied use cases. Trying to be more like Instagram or FB completely misses the point. 
Please bring back landscape video, and a dedicated creations tab with its own UI (like desktop).

conversations.title: Love this app worth the peace of mind
conversations.text:
I was honestly skeptical at first, but this app ended up saving years of my photos and videos that I thought were gone forever. I randomly found pictures from as far back as 2016 that I didn’t even realize had been backed up. That alone made the app worth it for me.

What I really like is how easy it is to use. Once backup is on, it quietly saves everything for you so you don’t have to constantly worry about losing memories if your phone breaks, gets lost, or runs out of storage. It also helps clean up space on your phone without making it confusing.

If you take a lot of photos or videos and you’re on the fence about paying for extra storage, I genuinely think it’s worth it just for the peace of mind. I’d rather pay a little than risk losing years of memories forever.

conversations.title: I Love my Google Photo App
conversations.text:
Google Photo Review
     I am a huge fan of Google photos and my wife gives me a hard time when I try to tell friends and family of its virtues.  I love the storage feature and the ability to sort by face, place or thing, excellent.  I just save all photos on my phone to a computer or some external memory then I can remove from the phone and rely on Google photos to have my pics at the ready.
      I am scanning old pictures into my computer therefore linking those to my Google photos as well.  In the properties, I can also change the date, which allows them to also be searched based on their age and to be found by the Assistant.
      I really enjoy the Assistant feature best.  I can't wait each morning to see what memory appears from the past and some albums are so good, I can share them as is.  Stylized pictures, animations, movies, I love it.  Facial recognition is excellent for finding anyone and I use it constantly.  Sometimes for people's birthdays, I use it to make an album on the person and put it on FB et al.
Love how you can search by almost any item,i.e. Beaches, birds, weddings etc, very useful.
     What would I like, captions for the albums, more editing features on most creations, however, it is terrific as is.  Thanks to the brilliant folks that have created this application!
        Have not much more to ask.  I do have large numbers of Albums and would like an easy way to search for them.  Right now, I have to scroll through them to find what I am looking for.  Still, I use This app more than any other application.  Thanks, don’t stop being creative, continue to improve!

conversations.title: Great app, some wishes for messaging
conversations.text:
The app overall has great features like facial recognition and even better TEXT recognition. If I take screenshots of important emails, I can find them again by typing up a word. It can even recognize some non-font writing it it is legible and consistent.

Something I wish was a little improved is the comments on albums. Sometimes they are a bit glitchy, and a notification will show up for a new comment but the comment itself will not appear on the album. 
It would also be nice if comments were available for partner sharing. 
Sometimes I wished there was more connectivity available between google hangouts and google photos - that way photos could be easily sent in a messaging format to others, rather than having to share from the google photos app. I could send photos from google photos via iMessage on my phone but it didn’t have the search options and albums. Having those available in the pull-up menu could also be handy because I make use of those sorting menus to be able to find photos faster and not have to scroll through years of pictures.
These are mostly personal wishes, less so complaints, and stem from unconventional uses of the app.

Overall it is a great app and great software.

conversations.title: Easy to access from all my devices
conversations.text:
One of my favorite Google apps. Keeps all my photos organized and easy to access from all my devices. I have always been a Google fan even though I prefer IOS devices. I like that you are able to back up when only on WiFi or using data. I share my data with others as I’m on a business plan so having this choice really saves on data.
Photography and gardening have become my passion the last few years. With this app, I am able to produce photos that are realistic and if I want to add some flare or erase something, their edit options are endless. 
Never again will you have to scroll and scroll just to find that one picture you took when you were on vacation. Just make an album for your vacation and the app will do the rest. All you have to do is enter in the search engine what picture you are looking for

conversations.title: L♡VE G PHOTOS - needs some improvements
conversations.text:
➊ Can you please make google photos available as a widget on the iPhone 
⮑(Like when you select photos on Apple’s camera roll app and click share, can you make it so there’s a button for importing to google photos - I’m not sure what it’s called but I know that apps like VSCO have this option.)

➋ Can you offer a way to sort images on Google photos? 
⮑ sometimes the app gets the date wrong so my photos are all out of order and it’s difficult to find what I’m looking for. (It would be nice if I could sort it by most recent or recently added) 

➌ Importing needs improvements. 
⮑ I use google photos to backup my pictures and right now, in order to import pictures directly to an album, I have to airdrop the pictures I want from my iPhone to my Mac then click and drag the pictures into the album I want on google photos. It’s very inconvenient but it works. However, my WiFi is under repair right now so airdrop is not an option and I want to add photos to my google photos album EXCEPT it’s too difficult to find them on google photos because they all have different dates! 

➍ Doubles! 
⮑ please offer a feature that identifies doubles of pictures and gives u the option to remove one of the copies! (Maybe in google assistant) This would be great - although, not necessary, but much appreciated if possible in the near future!

conversations.title: Love love love it!
conversations.text:
Google photos gives me great peace of mind that my photos and videos are always there for me and accessible. Gone are the days of worrying about lost or damaged flash drives and CD’s full of photos!
 
I have the Google Photos app on my phone (which is also my camera), so it’s super easy to upload all of them anytime — and bonus! it’s also super easy to clear up space on my phone (I can direct the app to delete photos from the phone that have been saved in the cloud). 

Google Photos makes it easy to share photos if I want to (I’m a private person, so I don’t share very widely). 

I love the versatility of the search feature, especially when I’m putting together an album or a collage, because I can search, say, “Emma December,” and it pulls forward all the images that contain Emma that we’re taken in December (after I have assigned a name to her face— also my choice). And if I have the location feature turned on when I take my photos, then I can search within Google Photos by location. 

Today I’m really excited because it seems like Google Photos has updated the app, so now I can see and select individual photos that were taken within a “burst” on my iPhone.

The unlimited storage is AMAZING. I take LOTS of pictures, and I know I can keep them ALL in ONE PLACE! It’s absolutely fantastic!

conversations.title: Overrated n disappointing and false AI abilities
conversations.text: This app was my fav a few yrs ago but had quickly become the worst experience I had. If it’s MY pics let ME sort n categorize them not you (app) it’s absolutely without a doubt, horrible! Ever since you claimed it knows me n can AI it all for me - is totally false. So how does a food entree pic qualify as a mountain when nothing like that no where near or part of the pic n location was in big city … so much for “smart organizing” the list I could give goes on n on n I can hardly ever find what I want r need. Plus it used to allow me to make my own files n put them there (move) from my main pic gallery (if I chose that option) to another pic file. Now I can NOT do anything that I want with any of MY pics/ notice they r MY pics not yours!! Truly saddened n disappointed you made it all worse instead of better … why fix something that was not ever broken? Worked for me and so many others … wish could have the previous version blended with the “dumb” (not so smart) version - then that would be a great accomplishment!

conversations.title: Don’t skip over this bc it’s here for everybody to read
conversations.text: I like the his app bc it give you so much storage. I’ve never found a app like this bc I always get notifications saying “your storage is full please delete some pictures “ but I never get a notification on google photos. I have way too much storage... probably more than I need. You also get an assistant were they make suggestions and stuff. I like this part bc whenever I am having trouble editing a photo, it dose it for me. There are also hidden features that I have also discovered myself. It also makes suggestions like “ you have 333 pictures, would you like to delete some?” And it allows you to go through the list and check off some pics that you would like to keep and then it deletes the rest. I have gotten so organized with google photos. I highly recommend this to ANYONE

conversations.title: My absolute favorite app!!!
conversations.text: I can’t express enough how much I love this app. I am a photo hoarder, between pictures of my children, family and friends, events I want to attend, crafts I want to create; with this app I never lose any of it. Before getting this app I was constantly backing my phone to my computer then to an external hard-dive (such a pain). I never have to do that anymore and I can access my pictures WHENEVER I want. If that wasn’t enough, you can identify each person and use the search to narrow down a picture you might be looking for (either a person, location, even a color or pet). Even more, the app will randomly generate movies (for something special like Mother’s Day or after an event like Christmas) including background music, collages, animations, color pops, and more. There is no app I boast about more. I would recommends Google Photos to EVERYONE!!!

conversations.title: Don't know what you have until you don't have it anymore
conversations.text:
Recently, our external hard drive crashed and we were devastated because every single one of our children's baby pictures were on it. So we sent it off to a data retrieval service, and was informed that none of the images were retrievable. We were heartbroken and very sad, until I remembered Google Picasa! So I opened the app and was ecstatic to find many of my children's baby pictures. Of course not everything was uploaded to Picasa because my husband did not download the app to his phone until after our external hard drive crashed. But we are very happy to have what we have.

So all I can say is, you don't realize how valuable Picasa is until you need it.

I have to admit, I have not used Picasa since I bought my iPhone. However, with the recent events I will be using it daily. So, thanks Google!

conversations.title: Love the extra features
conversations.text: This app is probably my favorite and most important on my phone. It continually backups photos I take so I never have to worry about losing photos if I haven’t backed my iPhone to iTunes in a while. It also provides search capabilities with grouping by person, activity, place and even things. I take a lot of screenshots of things and it has the ability to archive them so they do not clutter the main section. Probably what I like most though is the extra little things it makes like collages, movies, stylized photos and animations. While some of them are do not come out good, there are times where they give me something I didn’t even know I wanted. Most recently they provided me with a before and after collage and I just loved it. Would definitely recommend this app for anyone that cherish their photos and the memories behind them.

conversations.title: Mind Reading Photo App
conversations.text: My phone is an iPhone; my laptop is a MacBook Pro; my desktop is an iMac; and, I use my Apple Airbuds, iPad and TV almost daily. As a professional, mother of three, with no formal training in technology, I value the seamlessness and reliability of my Apple technology; I never think twice about whether or where my projects, emails, documents, etc. are on any of my devices... EXCEPT, MY PHOTOS ARE NEVER WHERE I THOUGHT THEY WERE! Of course, that’s my fault - I’m not blaming Apple. But, I’m officially DONE watching instructional videos, wading through advice from other Mac users, etc. GOOGLE HAS READ MY MIND! My photos are reliably available for viewing, incorporating, sharing, creating, etc. anytime on any device. The organization provided is intuitive and the options offered responsive - without limits! No more endless searches, no more frustration, no more anxiety - ONLY GOOGLE PHOTOS! Thank you, Google!

conversations.title: Horrible app
conversations.text:
Google may be amazing in some other areas but they definitely did a horrible job on Photos. I’m glad I didn’t buy any storage. It’s complicated to navigate, Lost a bunch of pictures and videos in the learning process, very frustrating app. 
Pics and videos take forever to upload to the cloud.  it’s been three days and still uploading two videos one for 15 minutes and the other one for 11 minutes. You can’t move the albums to organize them in alphabetical order. If I want to delete a pic from ur phone You have to be very careful when deleting videos and photographs is a mess. Also installed the app on a second iPhone and tried to upload some other stuff from that other phone to the same account, well guess what, is the same google account and the pics and videos on one are not the same as the other. Also when I deleted some videos from one of the phones it also deleted from the other cloud and that’s how I lost a bunch of videos. 
Anyway. I invite you to research a bit more before using. Thank you google for erasing some of my treasured memories!

conversations.title: Still amazing
conversations.text:
Started using Google photos years ago. Back when I first really understood how the cloud works on my iPhone. Finding out that once my storage on my phone was close to full, deleting photos from my phone that were backed up on the cloud would also delete them from my cloud and I’d lose the photo forever. Dumbest concept ever. I started researching an alternative and found this brilliant app from Google and it has been my lifesaver for years now. I’m serious. My photos are everything to me. I’m a self proclaimed artist. Be it writing, sketching, painting, or digitally- I love expressing myself without needing to use my actual voice. And photography as well as graphic designing make up some of my favorite forms of expression. If I lost any of my photos I’d be honestly crushed. To be able to go back through all my different phones, all the years gone by, right in Google photos albums, having everything there, that photo I took 5 years ago from the quiet walk bridge right before sunrise after an emotional hike with only myself and my phone, to have that photo sitting safely in my Google album, knowing it’s there, pulling it up when I need to remember, that’s everything to me. 
Nothings changed either. They now have a cap on the free part. Understandably. I gotta imagine that it’s beyond time they asked for some type of payment. The way they did it was pretty honorable and impressive. They don’t threaten to trash everything we’ve already saved, no matter it’s capacity (I truly have thousands upon thousands upon thousands of photos), they allow us to keep that, and they allow us an impressive cap before needing to request that we pay to continue to have everything backed up. 15 GB’s is damned impressive. For free??? You can’t beat that. It’s a universal, unlocked back up bank with 15 gb of space for free. You just can’t beat it. I’m changing phones again. New iPhone. And that’s why I’m leaving another review. Because I’m making sure everything is backed up and while I’m waiting for it to all be backed up I decided to give another rating and review. Because I love this app. It’s worth it. It’s awesome. It’s free. It’s honest.

conversations.title: Amazing Features that make up for what Apple Photos lacks
conversations.text:
I have been blown away by the extremely useful features Google Photos includes! I’ve been frustrated in the past with my photo library’s organization (or lack there of), photos of receipts for expense reports that I should’ve/needed to get rid of, duplicate photos, etc. Google Photos has features that help you maintain and organize your library!!

One of the coolest features of all, though, is the ability to search for photos by using a word. For example, I can search for the term “whiteboard” and Google Photos will show me all my photos that are of a whiteboard! It’s an intelligent feature that can go further than that, for example, searching for “diagram” or “architecture” will show me the subset of whiteboard photos that match those topics/categories!

conversations.title: Great App Except .....
conversations.text: I love their "Assistant", which configures videos, stylized photos, albums, etc.  It's wonderful!  You can download their creations, print them through third party labs, save the videos to discs, etc. The only thing that you cannot do, which I find truly disappointing, is send their albums to be printed as actual albums to include all the wonderful embellishments that they formatted. They do such a wonderful job with their embellishments, which include maps and arrows of times that you travelled. I soooo wish that all of that would be printable in a photo album as well. I would be willing to pay a nominal fee for this service. They do such a beautiful job, and would save you a considerable amount of time of having to add these embellishments yourself....many of which are not even available at photo labs because they're so customized. It is truly frustrating!!!!!

conversations.title: Thanks Google!
conversations.text: I love this app! After I took the time to become familiar with all of its features, I realized how great it actually is. Rather than going to get family pictures/videos done at some place that charges ridiculous prices for so few pictures, I can just take pictures/videos with my phone, edit them, order, and have them sent right from google at a very reasonable price. This app has saved all of the photos from every phone we’ve had in the past few years or so. Considering myself, 5 kids, and my wife... That’s a lot of different phones!!! I found pictures and videos that I thought I’d lost forever and there they were. Just sitting there waiting for me. Thanks google for such a great app. Myself and my family will continue to use and recommend google photos for as long as possible. 10 stars in my book!!!

conversations.title: DO NOT DOWNLOAD THIS APP!!
conversations.text:
So when you download this app and allow it to sync, it immediately starts doing that with all of your iPhone photos. Next, you’ll get an alert from Google that you are out of storage. So you think, easy- I’ll just delete all the pics from Google photos, I didn’t really want to use it anyways. Well you can’t do that. Not only does the delete button do NOTHING on an individual photo or group of photo, it seems that even in the best of times they don’t provide a way to bulk delete photos using your phone. You have to click on each individual photo. Then you go to the web app and it turns out there’s no bulk option there either AND the delete button doesn’t work. So in a panic because you can no longer get emails on your main email account, you have to pay to upgrade your Google storage. 

There’s also no way to directly contact Google about this. If you search Reddit this has been an issue for weeks. I’m so disgusted and frustrated. Do not, under any circumstance, download this app!

conversations.title: Photos are gone
conversations.text: I have over 12 years of photos gone. Just gone. I have had this app for almost a year now and I haven’t hardly had any issues with it. Except for this one thing that has happened like three times. I’ll go onto the app to look at old photos per usual and I decided I wanted to do this again a few days ago and photos from 12+ years are gone probably over 10,000 photos are gone. I have tried emailing and reaching out to the company multiple times and they still have not responded.
