I found out this has happened to other people as well and as far as I’m concerned, there’s no way to fix it. Yes, these photos had been saved in the app so there should be no reason that they just disappear like this. My mom has this app and she probably has around 20,000 or more photos on it right now and nothing has gone wrong for her. I’m just really hoping that Google photos can finally look at my emails and complain and fix this issue if possible.

conversations.title: Not bad, but could be better……
conversations.text:
Their AI protocols try to second guess one's intentions. For example, I sometimes take more than one photo and then the Google AI protocols will flag them and then a badge will appear at later time, because "it thinks" they're duplicates. I'll get a message, "Look what we found, two of the same or something like this"…… 

Hey I guess the geeks who mulled over this app design probably thought that it was just pure genius, well, I think it's just annoying!! And I'm not from your average Joe family either. I come from a scientific background and upbringing!! My dad is a retired research physicist and my mum's quite intelligent as well!!! Some people may have never heard of Argonne National Laboratory near Lemont, IL USA, but that's where my dad worked for 35 long years until he left in 2000. His area of specialty was superconductivity. I used to accompany him when he would go to the laboratory to check on his experiments. I'd ask all sorts of questions about what he was doing IN DETAIL!!! Anyhoo, 'nuff said!!

conversations.title: Deletes photos from your device.
conversations.text:
Update to review:
I got a response from the developer with links about my issues and how to resolve it, and typical of developers they did not read my review. They skimmed it to look for key words or used an AI to "read" it. The link they gave me was what I suggested in my review to new users.  I had already read through their help section and it is the same as the link. 


Original Review:
Make sure you disable sync if you want to delete photos from the Google drive but not from your device, otherwise it will also be deleted from your device. And you only have 30 days, if you haven't permantly deleted from Google drive, to recover it. There were several important videos I thought were saved on an older phone so it wouldn't take up space on my new phone and didn't think I needed it on Google drive. Not the case, if that old phone has your Google account logged on and it's set to sync and you delete from the Google drive, the photo or video is deleted. I would think if you delete from Google drive it's only from that drive and not from any and all connected devices. Also assumed it only synced if you add or delete from your device, and not from their drive.  Now I have to find a third party app to try to recover those videos. No thanks to Google.

So if you want to delete from their drive but not from your device, make absolutely sure "sync" is turned off.

Please let it sort back by either most recently added or by most recent picture or even alphabetically by album name. Any sort of structure or reasoning behind how the albums are displayed when adding a photo to it would be helpful instead of whatever is going on now.

conversations.title: GOOGLE PHOTOS = BEST APP EVER!!!!
conversations.text:
I’ve been using Google photos for about 6 years, and I have LOVED every minute of it! It’s really easy to use, and the absolute best option out there for storing photos. There are so many cool, helpful features to help keep my photos organized. And if you’re looking for a specific photo or video, you can just search for key words and it will usually come up. You can search “flowers”, “Chicago”, birthday”, “mug”, “wheelchair”, etc. You can type in a date or location and search that way, too. 

This app also recognizes faces, and you can label them, click on a person or pet’s face and name and see all the photos you have of that person. You can search “Dad”, “Grandma”, “Max” etc and they will come up that way too.

You can add photos/videos to albums, make collages, edit them, view “on this day” memories, hide photos of a specific person or pet, and hide photos of specific dates or locations, so that you only you see the memories you WANT to see. I am still learning about some of the awesome features and how to use them!

There are so many things you can do on this app WITHOUT needing tons of storage space! If my phone storage gets full, all I have to do is go to Google photos and click “free up space”. It deletes everything that has already backed up to the app (can be done over just wifi or data, you choose in settings), you don’t even have to sort through them at all. It usually doesn’t take very long to back everything up either. I have always taken ridiculous amounts of pictures and videos, and I save plenty from the internet too. And after 6 years of doing this, I have still not ran out of FREE storage!

Well done, Google. Hands down my favorite app out there! Keep up the good work :)

conversations.title: Ate 4 gigs of data backing up a 2 minute video
conversations.text: I'd love it if this app wasn't trying to be good at everything and just focus on being a good media storage source. While I love that I can store 3 years of photos and videos easily on my phone, this app is a serious data hog. Before using this app, make sure you have checked all settings regarding the apps data usage. Make sure you have turned off Its ability to use background data and check the "only backup videos on wifi" box. I was trying to clean up my phone quickly before an event Saturday and thought I would switch the "wifi only" mode off for a few minutes to get some of my videos backed up faster. (Because it literally takes this app DAYS to do it over wifi). In less than 5 minutes I got a text from Verizon saying I was almost out of data. The app hadn't backed up more than two minutes worth of video, but ate 4 gigs of data doing it. In less than 5 minutes. Now I am looking for other options to backup my media and delete this app all together.

conversations.title: so good for low storage
conversations.text: My phone only has 64 gb, so this is amazing for clearing up storage! I have google one, which gives me 100 gb of storage for about $2 a month! super easy to use, and comes with lots of benefits that my iPhone camera roll doesn’t have (rotates photos, easier to work, has tools like background erasers, etc)! my only complaint is there are some images / videos from my iPhone's camera roll that do not save / show up in google photos, so they still take up storage in my camera roll. There is also no easy way that I’ve found to upload pictures that are not in my camera roll. Along with this, i haven’t found a way to save pictures / videos sent in messages straight to google photos without saving to camera roll first. Regardless, though, this app is great, and worth your money if you decide to upgrade to google one!!

conversations.title: Google photos
conversations.text:
Excellent. Here is an outstanding circumstance....
    This app is intuitive, offers a broad enough array of tools and options to satisfy all my needs for a photo gallery and more. I loaded this app onto my iPhone 11 after i lost 80% of my photos upgrading to the new model. Work progress pics and irreplaceable pictures of my kids. I was furious! I had just backed up to the iCloud 2 days prior so i had no problem turning over my 7plus and watching the store associate FDR my old hardware. Lo when I saw that my new photo memory vault cheerily claimed my photos were now accessible but they clearly were not. 
    So a month later while working with one of our chrome-books, I remembered I had Google’s photo app on my old phone and boom! That baby synched up over 2400 pics and vid files! I am now made whole. Thank you Google. 
                 Ian Patrick Clark Sr.

conversations.title: Forcing Full Access is Invasive
conversations.text:
I used to use this app a lot for photo sharing, but I do not want to give FULL access to my ENTIRE photo library. 

One time, I allowed full access just to test it, and it immediately started pushing me to “back up” all my photos. Including NUDE PHOTOS onto my work email.

After all my personal photos got pushed to Google Workplace Cloud, I started getting charged for storage! I don’t want or need FULL STORAGE, I just wanted to share a few photos. 

Worse, when I tried to delete those nude photos later, I couldn’t find a straightforward way to remove them. I still have over 18k photos sitting in Google Cloud. Why? The newly added photos blended by date across all other thousands photos, so there was no way to Select All recent additions and delete them. 

Now, if I only give LIMITED access to my photo library, the app won’t allow me to upload any photos whatsoever. 

That feels suspicious and monopolistic! No other photo apps I use (IG, FB, editing apps) demand full access like this.

Google knows most people have a Gmail account, and they’re using that convenience to funnel users into giving up privacy to train their AI models on everyone’s photos, while charging them for storage.

When I try using the web browser version, the Google devs have “bricked” / closed up any possible way to share photos without giving them full access to my entire life. 

This is aggressive and privacy-unfriendly. It makes me dislike Google.

conversations.title: Love everything except too many notifications
conversations.text:
I love the Google Photo App: especially the memory collages, surprising special effect photos every now and then, finding similar pictures from the past and making a collage of them, and so on. I just find the notification alerts on the app VERY annoying when you open the app and there’s nothing to be notified of. Sometimes it’s trying to entice you to buy something, like ordering photos, albums, products, but sometimes there’s nothing, as if they just want your attention or want you to just open the app for no apparent reason. We already have a lot of other apps with notifications, we don’t need more distraction. Other than that, I LOVE the app. 😊
P.S. Trying to post this review; I was asked to type in a nickname. Any name I put there, is already taken. This is frustrating and discouraging!😡

conversations.title: So many working features
conversations.text: Really great app with tons of capability, including that the app automatically loaded the following for this review: “Automatically syncs my photos on a day to day basis, archives the uninteresting, stylizes the interesting, makes albums and collages by itself.... and a lot more” ... my biggest issue, though, is the feature that “curates” the pictures that it thinks I want to see on a slideshow. Most of the time they are good pictures, but every few months I scroll through and notice a great or memorable photo that I haven’t seen in a loooong time, that the slideshow just doesn’t serve up because it’s not in the curated list. It would be nice if there was at least a little more serendipity factor. Not for screenshots and whatnot, that’s understandable. But then it completely leaves photos that we took for a reason off the list for the family slideshow. This is meant to be constructive feedback.

conversations.title: Great, but improvements needed
conversations.text: I like this app a lot, I got it because I am a car enthusiast that collects in this case emblems/scripts/badges, and this app claims it can identify it. Editing this review, it has greatly improved at identifying cars, and parts. However, when I search a car, ex., 1968 Mercury Cougar, 1967 Chevy Camaro SS, 2017 Dodge/SRT8 Challenger 392 HEMI, when I search these, it used to tell me the year. Now it just brings up the newest things. 1997 Mercury Cougar, 2018 camaro, 2019 challenger, which is the most useless thing I've seen in quite a while. I got this app to identify stuff. Not to bring up ads of something essentially not at all what I want to see. That's BS. I want this thing fixed. The reason I can't delete it is because of free, so far unlimited storage. That's very helpful to me. But the ads - it isn't very helpful, however it isn't completely useless to parts, etc.

conversations.title: Love this app but needs a setting change or two
conversations.text: I love this app and have used it since I was 16. However, sometimes it will back up and upload the same photos several times and that is an enormous pain because you have to manually go through and delete them. I have looked for a setting to remove duplicates or only save originals and I can’t find one. I feel like that should be added to the next update because it would be extremely useful and a time saver. It needs this setting because I can spend hours trying to remove photos to reduce my storage and it takes hours. I can delete over 100 photos and not make a dent in my storage. And it’s my photos taking up my google storage. Please please please add this setting in your next update.

conversations.title: Picasa was better for editing and movie making but Google Photos is good job with facial recognition
conversations.text: I miss Picasa, but Google bought it and pulled the plug. Not nearly as many editing options in Google Photos. Uploading photos from my computer into GP is a real pain. If I have 50 photos to upload into GP from my hard drive it may take 20 attempts before they all upload. And they are saved by upload date, not by photo date. Bring back Picasa! PS. One thing I like about Google Photos is its capability of finding photos by subject, location or category. I wish I could manually add names of people in photos who don’t get picked up by the facial recognition software, such as silhouettes and photos from behind. I wish I can add text to photos to help me remember the locations and subjects, and to be creative with birthday and other celebration social media postings.

conversations.title: Albums
conversations.text:
I have now tried two times to create an album and google will not sync the photos. I created one album another time and didn’t have a problem, but this one has been a doozy. Tried to add photos to it last night, had 200 in the album, but it wasn’t showing up on my computer. When I went to check it on my phone again, it had completely cleared out the album. So I added 195 to it today (still don’t know which photos I’m missing) and it won’t show up on my laptop or on another app. I’m frustrated. It shouldn’t be that hard to take photos already on the app and put them in an album! 
I also can’t figure out how to delete multiple photos at once. It always just asks me if I want to move it to the archive. And I can’t add photos from the roll to an album, I have to go to the album and click add photos. There are also over 200 photos still on my phone’s camera roll because they won’t sync to google photos for some reason. Overall, not a great experience.

conversations.title: Very very good, but not yet great
conversations.text:
I love Google, so I may be a bit biased.  Google photos is a really good photo storage and photo sharing app.  I love that they offer unlimited storage, although it is at a decreased quality.  While original quality photo storage is available for a fee, it sure would be nice if Google made it free.  

I love the ability to upload a bunch of photos at once, but often some of the photos are skipped (unclear why).  I like that Google gives notice of the skipped photos, but often when it does this one loses the ability to automatically upload the ones that weren't skipped into an album.  After that, adding photos into an album isn't as easy as it could be.  How about a quick drag and drop feature?

I also love that Google automatically takes certain pictures and creates a computer generated copy with a special filter, frame, or makes a panorama of several photos, giving the Google Photo owner the option of keeping or discarding it.  

The photo search option is also really cool.  I can search thousands of my photos for pictures with dogs, or of Aunt Sue in the snow it Tibet.  It somehow does a really good job of finding these pictures.  It does make some mistakes, like adding wolfs to photos of dogs, but hey, aren't dogs descended from wolfs?  Overall the search, while not perfect, it is really good. 

Overall I would highly recommend Google Photos. Upload your photos from your phone, and if you lose or break your phone, your pictures will still be safe.  I would also recommend uploading the pictures from your computer for the same reason.  Then you can also access them from anywhere through the Google Photo app.

conversations.title: Just about perfect
conversations.text: The GOOG Photos app has been the best mix of everything I'm looking for in an online photo backup service: every picture, every video I take is available anywhere, anytime on any device. Then neat extras--animations, movie compilations from content I shoot, and how the service organizes everything fits my needs to a tee. The app is reliable and fun to use. It's also dead-simple to learn. The fact that I don't HAVE to buy extra GOOG Drive storage & that the pictures I upload are in nearly full resolution works for me. I've done side-by-side comparisons with original photos and I can't tell any difference. Lastly, the search--holy cow, the search-- best in the business. I can type in almost any minute detail into the search bar & GOOG Photos finds what I'm looking for. Highly recommended.

conversations.title: Loved it!
conversations.text: I got Google Photos on my phone to essentially replace the regular Photos since I liked the layout of Google Photos better. I haven’t had any issues since downloading it! It keeps my photos clean and well organized and the facial recognition software is 99% accurate. The only thing I would want more is maybe if they could add a feature where you could input more than one person in the search bar and come up with photos that had all of those people in them? Or maybe be able to search photos by date AND person. For example, inputting in the search bar “Max and Andy” could maybe come up with pictures of Max and Andy together. Or “Ruby 2020” comes up with pictures of Ruby taken in 2020? I just think that might be helpful. Anyway, overall I love this app!

conversations.title: Amazing for more storage!!
conversations.text:
Phenomenal app! I used to worry about my photos and videos taking my storage to, but Google Photos uses no storage after you safely back up all your photos to the app. After backing up your photos, you can delete them from your default app (like gallery or photos).
Google Photos is much different than the default app you may get on your phone. You can link certain photos to one face and search it up on the app. You will find every photo of that person on your device. 
Albums are extremely simple to create. The app will even suggest making a few for you when you take a lot of pictures in one location and time!
Another tool I love to use is looking up faces in your photos, like I mentioned before, and locations from your photos or even little things like searching the word “glasses” and it will show every picture in that place or with that object!
There are many other tools to help your photos, like filters for example. With the “assistant” tool you can see tips to help with your experience and little tweaks to your photos to make it pazzazed!!!
You can also make your own slideshow with FREE background music! It is so simple!
I’m so glad I use this app, it is so helpful and I hope you can use it successfully like I have!! :)

conversations.title: Great But Missing A Few Key Features For Super Users
conversations.text:
I love google photos and have over 120,000 backed up, and pay for a terabyte every month; here are the main features I wish would be developed in the future.

- Sort photos by upload date (not only chronologically; if you have a lot photos and you want to see what photos for example you uploaded or backed up Jan 1, 2010... (but weren’t taken on Jan, 1, 2010) There is no easy way to do this, nor can you use the search bar for “uploaded Jan, 1 for this option.

- Tag Items; this would help with sorting or seeing with photos are in an album or not in an album. There’s no way to easily tell if a photo is not in any album at all. (I tagged) apple makes this easy with “hide photos” as you can hide the photos you add to a specific album... and work on the remainder. Tagging or being able to group specific screenshots (ie. work, school etc.) in the archive would be great as well.

- Upload from Google Backup to Specific Album. (You can do this on chrome if you drag and drop to the browser > add to album when upload is complete, but it can get stuck if too many items are pending; you cannot upload to specific album on the backup app itself.)

- Album view needs a small thumbnail to the left view option just like google drive, the album view is a little difficult to sort through if you have 50+ albums.

- Love Picasa so much and it’s a shame it’s no longer a google product that is used. Google Photos needs a similar desktop companion, the backup to drive/photos only option is an awkward and finicky app that Picasa was so much better than in my opinion.

conversations.title: Fantastic - should have been using this years ago
conversations.text: I explored a lot more f different apps and was overly worried about photo quality.  In retrospect, I should have just gone to google photos right out of the gate.  Quality is top notch (even on the free setting) for everyone short of those with extremely high end cameras - for the rest of us google’s base quality is higher than our phones can generate anyway.  The real kicker is how it makes your photos accessible and useful.  The assistant regularly creates albums that are of interest and keeps “memories alive” by doing it.  The ability to search photos is phenomenal.  I had a crazy number of photos on my phone but never looked at them for years - we’ve gone through them more in the last 6 months with google photos than we ever would have otherwise.  Highly recommended.

conversations.title: Automated collages, videos, and animations 👌🏽
conversations.text:
Endless storage is my favorite thing about google photos!

A couple weeks ago was my sons 3rd birthday. Somehow google found all the pix of my son I’d taken over the past three years, but only the best ones (there weren’t any duplicated photos not even the 5 or 6 you take trying to get a good one) and created a “they grow up so fast” slide show, complete w music 🎶

conversations.title: Easy accessible storage
conversations.text:
I’m happy to have google photos mainly because I know that if my phone gets lost , broken or stolen  that my photos will be stored in my account. Even now having an Apple phone I have no problem accessing or saving my photos to Google Photos. 

I also like that I can have Google photos sort my pictures by who is in them. The facial recognition feature is very good. The suggestions Google photo offers to archive certain things is helpful and time saving for me. 

I really love all the special features like how Google Photos will make a video of a certain person or certain date or show other suggestions of how to do cool things with your photos. I always get excited to watch and see what memories Google photo chooses to use in the videos, etc.

conversations.title: Thank goodness for Google Photos
conversations.text: I found myself in the same situation many of you do. My phone was running out of memory and my pictures were at risk of being lost forever. Then I was told about Google Photos, so I downloaded it and set it for auto backup. I had priceless pictures on my phone of my mom and dad, who have both now moved on to heaven. These pictures could never be captured again. Then the day came. No choice but to get a new phone. Imagine how relieved I was to find ALL of my photos from the old phone waiting for me in Google Photos right on my new device. Thanks Google for protecting my priceless memories forever! If you don’t have this yet... don’t delay another second. Your priceless memories once gone can never be recalled again. You will be so thankful you got Google Photos and protected those memories forever!

conversations.title: Could be better
conversations.text:
In general, the automatic back up seems good, although I have noticed that a lot of my photos have not made it into the Google database.  The trouble is, I have no way of knowing which of my historical photos were successfully transported in which were not, without a one to one review which could take days.

The search function is very useful, though by no means perfect. The facial recognition is also suspect. I know I have scores and scores of photos of a particular individual saved, but only seven made it into the folder marked for that person.

You can take an unusually long time to back up a photo, and an equally unreasonable amount of time to download and save photo back onto your device. I wish the whole thing would act more quickly.

Finally, I wish albums would be stored alphabetically so that you could more easily find the album you were looking for when you want to add photos to it. As it is, you have a disorganized list of albums which very quickly becomes quite lengthy And you speed needless time trying to find the album that you want. This is made more complicated by the fact that Google photos creates its own albums with names that are not what you would have given them.

All in all, a good app that could be better, and perhaps it is the best currently available.

conversations.title: Best photo organization/storage app
conversations.text:
Just log into your Google account, take pictures as you normally would, and the app helps you store and access all the pictures taken on the phone. This is especially useful when I switch to a new phone, just log into Google account on new phone and bam! Instant access to all your photos taken with old phone. 

You can also search through your photos with the search bar. If you try looking up “car,” it’ll go through all your photos that have a car in the photo. It can even recognize some peoples faces. Doesn’t work all the time but this is definitely another great feature.

Only con I see is that you used to get unlimited storage but they're charging people for more storage after 50gb

conversations.title: Great product, but won’t upload everything
conversations.text:
I LOVE this app! Love how I can keep my photos, everything no matter what happens to my phone. I love I can find groups of pictures using a date, name, or face! I love how easy it is to use. I LOVE the “assistant” too! The assistant makes animations from photos, stylizes photos, makes great videos from my photos! And I LOVE how it takes a look back, 1 or more years on the same day—so nice to see! The only thing I wish I could change is that I WISH I could change the order of the photos I choose to make an animation! For some reason I can choose which photos, but not the order! I could make the animation flow better to my liking. Alas I don’t use that option as much because of this, even though it’s a great tool.

Update: there are several photos and videos that won’t upload to the website. I have tried everything. That’s pretty frustrating.

conversations.title: Poor app update
conversations.text: I am a longtime user of Google Photos, and the new update is disappointing. In the past, photos were clearly sorted by date for easy visual reference while scrolling through the feed. It used to be very easy to see what day a photo or group of photos was taken because there was a clear date header, and it was easy to select all photos from a given date simultaneously if desired. Unfortunately, now the photos all appear as one large group with no differentiation other than a date changing rapidly at the top of the feed as you scroll up or down. The new layout is disorganized, looks cluttered (especially for users with a large number of photos), and is much less user friendly. The only way I can truly see where one day ends and another begins now is to open up each photo’s metadata one at a time until I come to the next day. This is time consuming and defeats the purpose of a photo organization app. I hope the former layout will be restored.

conversations.title: Bait & switch + No way to sort by size
conversations.text:
Nice bait and switch by getting us hooked to the “free backups” of lower quality sizes, but then putting a 15gb cap. That cap is reached in days and then they stop you from sending and receiving email until you are under the cap. Holding you hostage until you pay. No thanks! Ain’t gonna work on me. I will just go delete the biggest items until under the limit, and stop backing up new items. 

This leads to the second issue. There is no way to sort items by size. At all.  Not even in non-mobile versions. You can’t list by details or any other sorting methods that should be available. This missing feature which should be considered a basic feature is likely missing so you can’t easily get under the 15gb free tier. They are trying to get you to just give up and pay for storage (that used to be free for lower quality remember). Well no thanks. Tip for others in the same dilemma: just find the list of just videos and go and delete the longest ones.

conversations.title: Disappointing
conversations.text: I just wasted 2 hours of my time selecting photos to add to an album. First of all, when I zoom in to a picture with the button in the bottom right, it is an automatic reflex for me to press the X in the top left to exit the zoom in. But no, that just reset me after I had selected about 300 photos. How about adding a safety questions “Are you sure you want to exit this album?” Secondly, when I was finally able to finish selected 500 photos to create an album, I created it and it was fine. Then I go to my home screen and when I return, the album is gone, not in the trash bin, not in the archive, it just disappeared and I couldn’t recover it. This was already frustrating enough but somehow I convinced myself to try again. 500 photos, I leave the app, comeback, 12 photos in the album I just created. I don’t know what kind of garbage this is, but I just wasted 2 hours just to not even be able to do something as simple as create an album. Thanks a lot, looks like i’ll be deleted this app 2 hours after getting it.

conversations.title: NOT A FAN OF THE LATEST FEATURE
conversations.text:
If Google Photos didn’t recently start automatically saving photos to your library that people send you on Messenger, no doubt I would’ve given 5 stars! I did on my last review.
Keep in mind, I haven’t looked into it yet to see if this feature can be disabled but I hope so! And for a few reasons...
#1 - personally, I don’t necessarily WANT TO SAVE EVERY random photo someone else decides to send you!
#2 - see #1 and with unlimited storage you get with Google Photos that can add to an already HUGE collection, adding to the amount of time it’s now going to take to sort through all those extra photos 
#3 - see #2 regarding taking more time to sort through photos - photos (or jokes, screenshots, etc) that may not be appropriate for every person you allow access to your Google Photos (or access to your devices with it installed) 
#4 - see #1-3 potentially inappropriate or offensive photos are saved ONCE THEY ARE SENT! NOT EVEN VIEWED! So if you’re like me & don’t go on messenger often, you could have photos saved from days or weeks before you even realize it!
PLEASE consider doing away with this feature, everything else about this app is awesome! But I don’t think this feature was very well thought out prior to implementing it. And if there is a way to disable, PLEASE SOMEONE LET ME KNOW!

conversations.title: Genuinely my best download of all time

conversations.title: still the best app overall to save and document all of your photos

conversations.title: Amazing Organization
