conversations.title: Great App but Google's Killing it.
conversations.text:
UPDATE: Google just announced they would be getting rid of the unlimited uploads in June 2021. This basically makes the app useless for me. I don't have a lot of money to spend on Google One, and Google estimated that I would run out of storage within a year. It looks like I'm going to remove it after June. It's no longer the savior of photo storage, but just another cloud storage app. Really disappointed.

Old Review: I found out about Google Photos last year and have been loving it! I am a photographer, and I have an older phone with 16gigs of storage, so I was trying to find a way to store photos I take with my camera so that I could show them to friends. But that tiny amount of storage on my phone made that impossible.
Enter Google Photos: Now I can upload my pictures to Google Photos on my computer, and see them on my phone, all while taking up minimum storage!
This would still be the case even if I had a phone with 256GB. I need that storage for other things, such as other apps, not full 25 megapixel photos. If I'm just showing friends photos on my phone screen, or them texting to them, I don't need that massive file.
So the shrinking is a bonus. A smaller file to put on social media or text to people, all while having all my photos in the palm of my hand and on any other device that has internet.
Even if you are an actual photographer and not just a smartphone shutterbug, I highly recommend this app.

conversations.title: Must have, truly awesome app
conversations.text:
I will sing this app's praises 'till the cows come home, as they say.
I have used this app for years, and I am thankful for it everyday. For one, it gives you the ability to store all your photos without taking up space on any device... As well as being able to access your photos on any device!!!!
Then, it adds in bonus features like becoming your timehop/memories app, but even better. It will recognize pets, people, children, relationships, and holidays and make you sweet little videos. It will take all of your random burst shots and make an animations. It will remind you what silly things you were doing years ago. And it's organization features are the tops.
I have had several phones, computers, wireless carriers, internet providers... I have never lost a photo or a video. Ever.

conversations.title: Love love love this app! Recommend %100!
conversations.text: If you’re like me and always switching phones or running low on storage fast capturing every important moment you need this app! It automatically backs up your photos & videos. So you can delete them from your camera roll & they're always stored away safe! Has facial recognition so it easily groups your photos for you to find easily by each person you take pictures & videos of. Easily clean up & delete blurred photos, accidental photos, etc. Even helps delete spam emails on your gmail account way quicker then doing it yourself. I havent found one negative thjng to say about this app and being using it for 4+ years. Just do yourself a favor and make your life easier by downloading this app! ☺️

conversations.title: It’s magical!
conversations.text: The facial recognition is amazing and it’ll group your photos by person (and pet)! You can also search your photos for random things like trees, clouds, mountains, etc. and it does a fantastic job pulling up all those things. It’ll read the tagging on your photos so you can search for locations too. All these things help you search for the photos you want to see very quickly. Of course don’t forget that by uploading your photos to Google you are basically putting them all in cloud storage and you basically have a backup... or delete them from your device for more room and instead just access them from the cloud. Finally it’ll occasionally take your photos and auto-create movies/stylized photos/animations/collages/virtual albums/etc. and the results are pretty cool.

conversations.title: The Best Thing Ever!
conversations.text: I love to take pictures, but phones come with various problems with that. One, they take too much space, two, there isn’t enough room for them, three, I can view them on one device and never see them again after my phone gives out, and four, I can never find the time to edit the photos or find good editing tools. However, this app fixes EVERYTHING! It’s a game-changer. It even creates movies, animations, and memory books for free! Now that’s only a bonus to the program! You can view it on any device, it takes almost no room, can store millions of photos, and it styles, edits, designs, and sorts all the photos for you! Another bonus is you can search up the place, year, or person in the photo and get accurate results! Now pinch me to make sure I‘m not dreaming!

conversations.title: I wish I’d known about it sooner
conversations.text:
Google Photos is the best way I’ve found to store and backup my phone’s pictures. It’s simple, intuitive and painless. The Assistant’s suggestions, albums and photo edits are fun and surprisingly good. The only problems stem from having to have internet access to show off snaps, and the need to reimport pics to the Photo Roll in order to use them in other apps (for example, avatars for social media or contacts). 
I also use it for my laptop, but as I haven’t verified that it stores all the metadata from each picture (as many others don’t), I’ve yet to transition my “good” DSLR pictures here exclusively. 
I’d love to see a function whereby certain folders would NOT be removed from my phone after archiving, as this would help immensely with pictures I take and need for work.

conversations.title: So much better than I would have thought!
conversations.text: Honestly Google Photos is amazing. I’ve never rated an app before but this deserves it. I find pictures so much easier and quicker than ever now! You can search for whatever you want a picture of— specific people in photos with you, places pictures were taken, and any other feature. I'm also able to save a ridiculous amount of storage just by using this app, and it’s so much better than the regular apple camera roll! 10/10 recommend. Google Photos even gives you suggestions on how you can edit pictures with filters, rotating them, and more! You will never stress about being unable to find a picture or your phone storage ever again, I can promise you that.

conversations.title: Great app
conversations.text: Such a great storage option! I ALWAYS had issue with storage and saving my photos but now that I have this app, I don’t have to worry about losing my photos ever again! I love that I don’t have to pay 100 dollars a year for a storage limit. This app is a life saver. I don’t have to worry about uploading my photos myself because as soon as I take them, google photos solves that for me. I also love the cute little animations that the app creates. The only reason I gave it four stars is because there’s a glitch or issue with trying to search for old photos! Every time I search a year or a month up to look for photos, I’m only allowed to scroll past a certain point. When I try to scroll and load older photos, the app takes me right back up to the top! I wish for this issue to be fixed because I can’t search for old photos anymore!

conversations.title: Lacking major features
conversations.text:
There may be several issues I’m having where I’ve made some error or overlooked a “workaround / life hack” to accomplishing my needs, but so far, here are a few of my frustrations:

Doesn’t identify and help clear duplicates based off metadata and/or image content.

Doesn’t auto suggest best pic of group.

Makes movies and collages based off date and time and location, not content.

Suggests random crops to images that make no sense.

Can’t create a photo database with filters and tag words the way I need.

Keeps suggesting I share private images with family. NO! Why would I?

Let’s me download some images and videos, but not others.

Takes a long time to download from the cloud... which cloud? Who knows!

Won’t necessarily upload in background.

Can’t give 1-5 hierarchy rating to the quality. 

Assistant doesn’t provide consistent offers.

Won’t clear the 40,000 images from my iPhone and iCloud as instructed.

Constantly given “cannot backup 800 photos” cues, but no real explanation as to why / why not.

Creates duplicates in my google drive. 

Little control over parameters.

Doesn’t read text in photos.

Search feature overlooks certain words and phrasing must be identical when searching.

Pretty amazing photo ID at times, horrible at other times.

Doesn’t feel like advanced AI.

Can’t remove photos from iPhone and leave them on icloud.

Can’t plug-in to certain apps.

conversations.title: Google is so smart!
conversations.text: I just uploaded all 100,000 of my photos over last 20 years to Google Photos at high resolution (up to 16MP), which has unlimited quota.  Now I can browse and search by people, location, object, and even activity, in a snap!  This is light years ahead of the search capability of iCloud or other online photo albums. Also, I repurposed old iPads and put them in my room and my parents room so that we can use them as smart photo frames which show my family photos in Google photos via SoloSlides app.  It is so cool to see a baby photo of my kid taken 10 years ago!  Google will auto detect and group faces, auto update the photo albums as you take more photos on iPhone and sync to google photos.  I am looking forward to more smartness from Google.  Nice work, Google Photos team!

conversations.title: Amazing App
conversations.text: After repeated attempts to delete, technical support, hair pulling and nail biting weeks trying to access my ICLOUD I finally gave up and called my carrier to have them just go in and delete all my pictures in my iCloud because I have already deleted all from my phone but I still keep getting that dreaded message that says "my iCloud is full" I was fed up just delete it. I was placed in touch with a tech that told me about Google app and told me to download it and forget about the iCloud. I wiped my phone and started it from scratch and have been happy ever since!!! The Google app downloaded pictures I had on my iPhone and pictures I thought were lost forever!!! I'm so thrilled I have this and will never think or anything other than google after this experience!!! Way to go Google!!!

conversations.title: Thoughtful
conversations.text:
This app really tries to connect thoughtful memories of you and your family. Sure, its not perfect. But for an automotive story, it can create real emotional moments and produce moments you haven’t thought of. 
A lot of us sum up our lives with emojis or gifs. Google photos seeks to find a way to bridge the gap and provide us with a FREE way to transgress the boundaries of social media and capture the emotion of every moment we experience.
I adore the fact that Google reminds me of birthdays and anniversaries no matter the importance. And they celebrate the moment with a quick story that you can adjust depending on your comfort or status. 
I’ve never been disappointed with Google products and this I just another step in the evolution of an amazing service.
Thank you Google, for helping me remember the memorable moments

conversations.title: Some things you should know
conversations.text: First of all, this is a great app. But I wouldn’t go crazy over it. For one thing, if you have a slow internet service, it will take forreevveer to upload photos. I’ve had this app for over two weeks and so far I’ve had to manually select longer videos to get them to upload, and after that it takes about five hours plus to upload eight videos. That’s just my WiFi, but I’ve been having other problems too. You should know INTERNET IS REQUIRED TO VIEW VIDEOS. I deleted about 100 videos and was super excited that it freed up about seven gigabytes(the great thing about this app), but then it told me I need internet to watch my videos. Which is fine if you have access to WiFi wherever you go. Photos can still be viewed. This app would probably be a lot more enjoyable with faster internet. Videos take a while to load, plus you pretty much have to leave your device on for fifteen minutes if you want to load an app-made video. However, if you have fast internet, and internet everywhere, this is a great app.  It takes your photos and videos and makes movies, makes suggestions for albums, lets you share photos, and even has photo collages and animations from photos or a video segment. You can also make your own videos, etc., but another issue I’m having is with albums. When I try to add photos to my own album, they  don’t stay in the album. I added about 300 photos to an album and found when I reloaded the app that only three actually remained. I tried a few more times, with smaller amounts, too, but it pretty much just adds whatever it wants. I guess it’s more of a summarizing thing. If it makes an album of a certain day or vacation, (yes, it’s knows you went on vacation), it only takes certain photos in an album.  There are many advantages to this app also.  Your photos can be accessed from the internet (but not by anyone else!), and there are bonuses. One bonus is what’s called Google Lens. It scans a photo of almost anything, a map, a landmark, an old car, tells you what it is, and looks up information about it on the internet!  So all in all, it’s a pretty great app. Especially with a good internet service. 🙂

conversations.title: Google Photos has made me a happier person.
conversations.text: This app is phenomenal in so many ways. Over the last year, I’ve uploaded ALL of my life’s photos into this app, including scanning all of my old school photos from childhood (and even photos of parents, grandparents, etc). An unexpected outcome is that because of how easy it is to find photos with this app, I actually find myself looking at old photos on the regular and enjoying the happy memories they evoke. This is an outcome that would just simply never happen if all my old photos were to have stayed in a box in my garage. In short, it would not be an exaggeration to say that using Google Photos has made me a happier person by helping me stay reminded of all the great things I’ve experienced in life.

conversations.title: It is so helpful! 👍
conversations.text: Google photos is the best app to take care of your photos. It makes movies of fun times,  helps you manage your space and it’s all in one place. You can assign people to pictures and then you can look up pictures by picking on their profile which makes it easier picking out you profile pics for friends and family while also being helpful if you want to just look at specific pictures of someone it’s all in one place. I definitely recommend this app. And by the way I am just a normal person who doesn’t pay stuff for apps and is always struggling finding good apps and games that work and fit your needs, so I’m not that bias person who likes stuff just because they bought the premium.

conversations.title: Best app to backup pictures
conversations.text: I LOVE that you can choose unlimited storage for free - I wouldn't use the app otherwise. The quality is also fantastic considering the fact you're not paying for the higher resolution backup (which is available). This is my go to app as I take a lot of pictures on my phone and I don't have the space to hold all of them + videos. I love how I can also backup pictures from any other device by logging in to my account and it automatically sorts the pictures by their dates & months so it's super easy to scroll through your history. I also find it a nice touch that when you upload similar pictures the Assistant will create cute animation gifs of your pictures and you can fix the lighting with one touch in some of your darker pictures!

conversations.title: Convenient, but Sometimes Annoying
conversations.text:
It's very nice that I no longer have to back up my photos to my computer, but I don't like the fact that if I back up my photos in "original" quality, than it takes up space on my Google Drive and Gmail. It also has several random things that it won't back up, even though it's a perfectly normal photo. 
Some things I do like, though, is that it can make animations for you, or stitch photos together to make a panorama, or make movies and albums, all automatically, and the. You can just save it if you like it. You can also easily search your photos by keyword or date to easily find what you're looking for so you don't have to go scrolling through everything.
Overall, I'm very pleased with the product, and it's probably the most useful app on my phone that I've downloaded.

conversations.title: Definite Help to storage problems and more
conversations.text: Well, to start off I was having storage problems and the choice was to either buy more storage, or find some app that’ll store things for me and boy am I glad I picked the cheaper option Google photos might be the best app they’ve ever made tbh. Not only does it help with storage but the apps little helper has this program in which it puts together pictures and either makes a collage based on date and/or people in the picture or makes an animation based off of pictures taken in a row to the point to where it looks like it’s moving though some may believe it’s kinda intrusive but I’d rather this over literally any app because now I can delete the app and still have the pictures on google and all i have to do is sign in.👍

conversations.title: The best photo app for this Mom!
conversations.text: With 4 kids - well adults actually - in 4 different cities, Google Photos is the best way to store, organize, share and edit photos. With it’s “on this date” feature, a quick collage will pop up from your timeline that you can instantly share with family and friends. Those shared memories are so important to staying connected. Also it makes photos so easy to find on the timeline with the slide bar. It doesn’t matter which device you are currently using, you can find your photos quickly anywhere and share to many apps/programs or to edit. After using many other photo organizing apps including Adobe, this is the most streamlined, user friendly app. I looooove Google Photos.

conversations.title: Great app!
conversations.text:
The best cloud storage for photos! It automagically backs up every photo on my mobile devices. And it’s free! With a small caveat.... the photos have to be under a certain size. That’s not a problem since I’m not aware of a cell phone that exceeds those size limitations with the possible exception of panoramas. 

That alone would be a killer feature, but the goodies don’t stop there. Once in the cloud The Goog sorts the photos in a number of ways, if you allow them to they’ll recognize your people so you can search for a photo of a particular person. It will make animations of sequential photos so you get a time lapse of a given event. 

You can even edit your photos with filters or automagically and I’m pretty impressed by how good they are (I’m not usually a fan of auto modes for photography).

conversations.title: Google photos is the best there is
conversations.text: When it comes to photo saving/storage you will not find a better app than Google photos. You're always guaranteed you're photos are safe, protected and stored properly. There is unlimited storage that you can't find anywhere else, especially when it comes to unlimited Photo storage that is free. With Google Chrome, your storage photos are at your fingertips anytime you want them. itother cannot be Google photos When it comes to Moments, that app has not worked great for me since the beginning, I have not liked what so ever and it's not at all what they thought it was going to be. Thank you Google photos for being the best number one at what you do and being there for us. Rhonda Holland

conversations.title: Great with a few major issues
conversations.text:
I love the app even though I have to pay for storage. I really like that Google’s AI let’s me search for specific faces or things in a particular photo, it’s very useful. The pictures seem to load quickly when you need them. 

I dislike that photos download onto a computer as .heic files and I wish there was a way to change this so they would download as JPEGs. It’s disappointing that there’s no locked or private album feature, similar to Apple’s hidden photos. 
The biggest issue I continue to run into with the app, however, is that it just won’t delete photos sometimes. No matter how many times I go into the app, delete a batch of photos, and even empty the app trash, they continue to come back. I’ve closed and restarted the app over and over again trying to delete photos but nothing works. I know it’s not a syncing issue between my devices because the photos are deleted from my phone and I don’t have any other devices connected to my Google Photos account. The same photos I’ve deleted many times over continue to show up in my app. 

This is a major flaw, it’s very annoying, and it makes an otherwise great app lose at least a star for me.

conversations.title: Almost necessary feature missing!
conversations.text:
I like the app! It’s nice. It syncs incredibly fast and for someone who needs my photos on both my laptop and phone it’s wonderful, considering iPhone’s small iCloud size (it stops updating on the pc end when full) so I’m very thankful for this!

However. There is a necessary feature that’s missing. Album syncing. I don’t believe it would be that incredibly hard to implement, as Google photos has already included the ability to sync favorites—so, wheres the album coverage? I put a lot of my photos into albums and having to re-put them back is extremely tedious, especially considering I can do it with one click for favorites. 

If this feature is added, I’ll 100% come back and change the rating to 5 stars, as that seems deserving!

conversations.title: 6 years and no complaints
conversations.text:
Obviously no app is perfect; however, this app has came the closest app to perfect for me. I have had this app for almost 6 years. I've been able to see how my life and friendships have changed over those last 6 years. I have kept almost every photo that I have taken of my loved ones and whenever I am sad, I am able to look back on those memories.

There is limited space without pay which is why I upgraded. However, that limited space is enough for most people. I may be a memory hoarder though. I have over 50,000 photos saved on here yet I still am not even close to having all my storage filled. Also, it's at a low cost. I believe $2-$3/month for 1 tb! That's a really good deal for what this app offers.

Not only that, but they have a system which organizes certain faces into their own category. Whenever I want to see the progess of a certain person, I just go there and see. It's amazing how I've seen so much of my family and myself grow and change over the years.

If you're looking for a photo gallery that will help you save space on your phone or computer, organize faces, and give you memories to reminisce on, this app is the one for you!

conversations.title: overall great app
conversations.text: i had about 47 GB worth of photos on my phone to where it was filling up most of my storage, so google photos helped out SO MUCH with having it be able to take away the amount of storage taken up. however, the only problems i had with it was that there were a lot of photos out of place than where they were normally on my photos app so i would have to search around for it instead of knowing where it usually was. the other thing was that i had a lot of my photos either in a specific album or my “favorites” but that doesn’t transfer over to google photos which causes me to have to go through and select them all again, which took quite a lot of time. if i were to suggest something, it would just mainly be for those two things, otherwise it is an overall great app!

conversations.title: Best photo app and storage available. More importantly I think Google will be around for awhile.
conversations.text:
After using various startups to store my photos and videos in the cloud I find Googles app to be the best. Many of the startup, while developing elegant platforms have failed...wasting my time and money in the long run.  I am somewhat of an Apple fanboy, but their approach and solutions are sorely lacking. 

Google has better data search, facial recognition and interface. Google's "Assistant" is well done and adds much value. All of these services fail at deduping properly. Can someone please get serious about solving this problem. I can't believe it's that difficult, but my guess is that it is not cost effective. All that being said I am thus far happy with this app and give it 4.75 stars...rounded up to 5. 👍

conversations.title: I recommend this app
conversations.text:
This app is wonderful. I have an iPhone and I don’t think much more needs to be said about why I need this app. 

The only issue I had was easily and quickly resolved with a quick Google search. The issue I had was that when the app was finished backing up my photos, I’d go to free up space and the number of items to delete wasn’t the same amount of photos I had in my phone’s “photos.” I assumed it was because the files were too big but I didn’t know how to change that. Google told me the steps for this which are: open the app-assistant-drop down menu-settings [top righthand corner]-back up & sync-upload size-original. 

When you select original size, it will tell you that doing this will go against your quota. I selected “original size” anyway but did not notice a change in storage space within the app. Obviously this resolved my issue and it was not difficult to find a guide for doing so. 

I only use this app so I CAN have space on my phone and don’t really use it for anything else but I do like a lot of the features you see when you open the app. 

I recommend this app all the time and will continue to do so because it has impressed me a lot.

conversations.title: Continuously Improving
conversations.text:
Google Photos is an ever-evolving app that consistently pushes the boundaries of what a photo management and sharing platform can do. With each update, it brings new features, enhancements, and optimizations, making it a top choice for users seeking a versatile photo app.

Pros:

	1.	AI Magic: Google’s powerful AI algorithms automatically categorize, tag, and organize your photos, making it incredibly easy to find specific moments in your collection.
	2.	Storage Options: The generous free storage for high-quality photos and videos is a standout feature, especially for those with limited device space.
	3.	Seamless Sharing: Sharing albums and photos with friends and family is a breeze, and the collaborative features make it perfect for events and group projects.
	4.	Search Capabilities: Google Photos’ search functionality is a game-changer, allowing you to find photos by entering descriptive terms or even object recognition.
	5.	Editing Tools: The app’s built-in editing tools are handy for quick adjustments, and it even offers suggestions for enhancing your photos automatically.

Cons:

	1.	Privacy Concerns: Users should be mindful of the potential privacy implications of Google Photos, as it relies heavily on Google’s AI, which may raise data security concerns for some.
	2.	Changes in Free Storage: Be aware of Google’s storage policy changes, as they have evolved over time. This could impact how you manage your photos and videos.

“Continuously Improving” is a fitting review title for an app that never stops getting better. Its robust feature set, AI-powered organization, and seamless sharing capabilities make it an invaluable tool for managing your precious memories. However, potential privacy and storage concerns should be kept in mind while using the app.

conversations.title: New search tool blocks you from accessing your own photos
conversations.text:
The search tool doesn’t work anymore for people in healthcare. I am a pathologist studying for hemepath boards, so I have a lot of photos of notes I take during didactics. This used to be the best app for searching through old photos. Recent updates have been so bizarrely paternalistic that it will block access to your own photos and claim you’re [seemingly] not smart enough to look at them. Yes, your own photos. 

I am not joking. 

Both vague medical terms like “liver pathology” or specific terms like “hepatocellular carcinoma” will provide no results and trigger the AI search function instead. The AI will then tell me that it can’t diagnose health conditions and I should talk to a doctor, despite me already being a doctor, blatantly not asking any medical question, and simply trying to search study material within my OWN PHOTOS. There is no option to do a normal search anymore without the Google gods triaging your photos.

conversations.title: Great photo storage
conversations.text:
Love the free photo storage. If you already have a gmail/Google account there is no reason to not utilize Google photos.
I love that you can “free up space” by deleting g your photos that are already uploaded that way you always have room to take more pictures! No more annoying “low storage” warning. 
You can also edit your photos, and make animations with photos and videos which is a rad feature.
The app has face recognition so you can label and group together pictures of the same person and easily search for them by name/whatever you labeled then as. Some examples are like if you wanted to see all the sunset photos you have, you would search “sunset” and they would all come up. You can do it with people too once you go through and label them which is super convenient.
I love being able to organize my photos by album- and speaking of albums, the app creates little albums for you for certain dates or events that it thinks you may want to see. It’s neat to see what the app chooses and “thinks” you might want to see put into an album. 
There are so many other features on this app too- to many to list.

conversations.title: Google Photos lost my photos... not a reliable service or app
conversations.text:
I first started using Google Photos when I bought a Pixel 2 phone. Loved it! I immediately loaded Google Photos on to my iPhone and finally had an app and cloud service that seamlessly integrated my iPhone pix and Pixel 2 pix. So far so good...

Fast forward 18 months... was cleaning up my photos during self-quarantine and noticed that many, many photos taken on Pixel 2 phone are now missing from Google Photos. My trip to Vienna and Venice, perhaps only 25% of photos remained; ditto for my trips to NYC, Pittsburgh, Seattle, San Francisco, LA, Tokyo. All the great memories are now gone/missing. Ironically, all my iPhone photos that are backed up on Google Photos are still there!

Searched online and found many people with similar experiences and all said Google support was no help. I too reached out to Google support and find their help so far to be useless: all cut and paste suggestions such as did you check archive and trash? Did you log into Google Photos under another account...etc. 

Frankly, I am very disappointed at Google’s callousness and lack of responsiveness to this problem given how important photos are to everyone.

Our photos are our memories, our emotional connections to places, people, time, events, and experiences. Memories make us human and define who we are; you can lose my emails but you can’t lose our memories.

conversations.title: Amazing Service Until Recent Update
conversations.text:
I have been using Google Photos for years. It’s the best photo service around. I love the fact that you can archive photos after sorting them. It’s super easy to share, sort, download, and see all your photos. My family all uses Google Photos so we can easily share albums with each other. I even pay for more storage, that’s how much I love this app. 

However, after the newest updates I want to cancel my subscription and find something else. I HATE how all my albums are now under “Collections” instead of being in their own tab like they used to. I HATE the fact that when I go to add photos to an album, it used to be in order by the album that was edited most recently, now it’s random with all my shared albums being at the bottom. So now I have to scroll through my list of a million albums just to find the one I’m looking for. It’s made photo sorting so much harder. I wish I had never updated the app.

conversations.title: Love this app💯
conversations.text:
I seriously love this app! It allows me the ability to be able to store ALL my pictures & videos in 1 place so that I don’t have to search & wonder where I stored this photo or that video, also it allows me to store them somewhere besides my phone, & that way I have all the space on my phone I need! I would DEFINITELY RECOMMEND this app to anyone that wants to keep all the sentimental photos & videos they want & love. Besides having to delete them, because you’ve ran out of space. You can also make different albums to separate them the way you want & put titles on the albums! 
Example:{ Baby’s 1st Birthday} You can add different people to your collection & name that person too! There’s just so much google photos offer & again I’d advise you to at least try this app!

conversations.title: Google is our friend!
conversations.text:
There are so many things that could be mentioned about the amazing work Google creats everyday to make life easier for us, that makes it hard to express how wonderful it really is to be able to solve problems quick and officiant. Google photos is pretty amazing overall except of one thing. I usually have a hard time having access to my photos IF, I, for instance need to upload A photo onto a certain website! In other words if I am in need of dragging a file onto a website. I wish I could get some help to find out weather I'll have to download all my photos one by one on my device and then choose a file to upload or are there other solutions available as well that I'm not aware of! .
Thank you Google as always

conversations.title: Love it to pieces. Only wished it was a flat fee!!!
conversations.text: I can't say much beyond what people have raved about this app. It's absolutely great. It's instantaneous. It's easy. It's dependable... for the most part.  I have lost edited Assistant Movies on several occasions. It creates really awesome movies capturing a day or week of events and even adds in playful music. You can edit them by changing the song, what vids and pics you want to include, and other fun details. But it also crashes by not saving movies when you try to select the segment of the video you want; e.g. It may choose 4 sec of the end of a video and you may prefer 12 sec from the beginning. It crashes all the time when you try to save your edits. The other thing is to honor your customers by allowing them to do a one-time purchase of an allotted storage size versus month to month charges.

conversations.title: Seriously the best!
conversations.text: First of all I never rate apps but this one is exactly what I was looking for!  I needed to remove photos from my phone but didn’t want to because then I’d have to go to my computer to look at them. This app allowed me to remove them off my phone but still keep them on my phone!  I freed up 10GB of data using this app. It does an amazing job sorting your photos, making albums and keeping all your pics right at your fingertips!  The only thing you should know is that is can take days to back up all your photos if you had a lot like me. Other than that once they are all backed up it takes no time to stay on top of backing up your photos.  It was able to recognize my dogs, friends, family, places, things etc. super awesome app!  Thanks!

conversations.title: Be aware
conversations.text:
The app is good in that it backs up your photos but it runs in the background and I didn't realize but it ate all my data even though I was connected to wifi. Had to turn off cellular usage which means it won't work if not connected to wifi. Also, I was low on my phone storage capacity and it freed space for me but then it creates animation and photo collage and I find the storage unstable ( an example is I free storage by deleting backup photos and when it loads check my storage it will show I have 10 GB of free space the next day I'll get a message that I am low on space again and need to free more storage it will turn out I have less than 1 GB 
I'm afraid to delete the app and loose all the photos that already backed up

conversations.title: It Just Won’t Work!
conversations.text: I am trying to create a shared album for a family trip we took over the weekend to share the photos with the family, and there are so many issues! First, it wouldn’t let me upload the photos to where I could share them. I went to share and it popped up with a screen informing me it was saving recent changes. I let that stay there for fifteen minutes and it did absolutely nothing. When I tried to share the link, my boyfriend said the album was empty. So I reuploaded ALL of the photos, and he STILL says the album is empty. When I went back into it, I found that there was at least one missing image, which is the MAIN IMAGE I am trying to send! When I went to upload it, it didn’t even show up in the list of photos that I could upload from, so I had to duplicate the photo in my personal album, and that allowed it to show up. However, when I went to upload it, it went to an “uploading file” screen and won’t actually upload the ONE photo!

conversations.title: Great app!
conversations.text:
I have found Google Photos to be very helpful with my picture storage. It has allowed me to keep hundreds of photos (with high quality!) that I would not have been able to save otherwise.

My only concern is that of a certain quality that is ignored in the account-linking feature and could hopefully be added one day. When you transfer photos from one account to the next through linking accounts, you have to take new pictures of people (after changing the backup settings) just to have them shown in the "People" (also "Things", "Places", etc.) category on your other account. If not, then those folders will never include them.

Other than that, this is a very useful application to have and I suggest you try it out!

conversations.title: Privacy invader!!!
conversations.text:
Everyone is praising this app, it’s a good app, it has lots of organizational and creative features, but it has a huge fault: invasion of privacy. Once you install this app on your phone and start backing up your pictures from your phone’s photo app, there’s no turning back. 
I toggled off the photos’ back up & sync and the Google Photos app still backs up the photos from my phone. 
Further, whenever I delete pictures from the Google Photos app, it deletes them from my phone too. This app sticks to your phone, it gets your pictures and all the data, then you can’t delete them. They should, at least, have an option where you could choose whether to delete them from your phone or not.  It’s just unbelievable!!!
I also tried to log out from the app, just to make sure my photos don’t back up & sync anymore, after switching off the back up didn’t work, but I ran into another problem: I can’t find the log out button within the app. Then I tried to just delete the app from my phone without logging out, but I got this message saying if I delete the app, I lose all the data. 
I don’t know what to do, I feel like I’m stuck with this app, it bothers me a lot! I didn’t realize what a tight control Google has over your phone once you allow it to access your pictures.

Update: I figured out you can disallow them to access your pictures from your phone settings....but still, this should be an option available within the app. 
Still disappointed that I can’t just delete the pictures I backed up without losing them from my phone too. I’ll just save them all on a Flash drive then delete them from the app and retrieve them later from the flash.

conversations.title: creepy smart
conversations.text: Once I discovered you can search your own pictures for theoretical things it was on. I probably spent 2 hours (I’m sure someone who works at Google could tell you exactly how long I spent with a few keystrokes) searching for things like: tire, cat, mirror, purple, can, art, cloud, parallelogram. Nothing short of mind blowing. Also makes gifs from photo bursts. I feel like easily making gifs from my phone elevates me from “average lurker” to “guy who could contribute to the internet maybe someday.” Aside from that it handles all the standard photo app duties as you’d expect from Google; solid processing, intuitive controls, photo editing adequate for a hobbyist, plain Jane gui lacks polish. Plays nice with Apple for the most part.

conversations.title: Lost every photo taken after years. Multiple backups gone.
conversations.text:
I have used this app to back up photos taken on different phones, etc. For years it worked great and I could always download my old pictures onto a new device. Suddenly, over 7 years of pictures were gone with no trace - not in the trash, or archive or anywhere, and I was left with nothing other than what I had taken with my current phone. 

There is no way to resolve issues other than asking the community, which unfortunately has just told me to check my trash and prevent my question from being addressed properly. 

I wish I had known this was a possibility or I would have backed the pictures up to a hard drive. I don’t want to complain - but a backup service is exactly what this app was supposed to be, and it left me with nothing. Google will not answer anything now that everything is missing, so I’d like to warn other people of what I experienced.

conversations.title: Google Photos
conversations.text: I thought my photos were gone because I lost access to my account and I was so surprised and continue to be that Google found them and collaborated with my other accounts and I have +6,000 pictures. I cannot begin to express my gratitude because my photos are part of my life. Also, I love the other features within the app including the utilities, the suggestions to help my photos stay cleaned up and organized. I like how have so many choices in sharing and I really liking popping on every day to see what was created just for me. I’ve cried happy tears watching the short videos and I have been amazed at the beautiful color pop pictures. Thank you Google Photos! I have and will continue to recommend your app to everyone!

conversations.title: Confusing…
conversations.text: Wanted to free up space on my iPhone and google pics says that I could view my pics at any time.  But when I hit the free up space tab it said all my photos would be deleted from my iCloud!!! WHY?? Where do they go? To free up space the pics go into their clouds, right?  So if my pics are already backed up in my iCloud and no longer using space on my phone, why does google photos want to delete them from my iCloud?  My iCloud is not full, I have 2 tb on my phone and only used 15% of storage.  So I don’t get it… what I really want us to remove duplicate photos like it used to do a couple years ago. Idk what happened or if I’m just missing it, but I can’t find the tab that says remove duplicate photos like it used to have.  It was better before, whatever they did only made it harder and less helpful.

conversations.title: great app, one small thing
conversations.text: this is an overall great app, it’s so easy to save space and search for so many things with different categories. love how easy it is to select things and organize into albums and add things to albums after they are already created. there is one thing though, after having added a photo to an album, and i am going back through looking at it, if i decide i don’t want the photo backed up anymore, there is no way to delete it straight from the album. In order to delete that photo you have to go back to the main camera roll and scroll through to look for the picture which is a major waste of time. It would be very nice if there was a delete photo option while inside of an album.

conversations.title: Highest recommendation
conversations.text: I use this app to back up my photos in addition to iCloud Photo Library. I don't mind paying a few bucks a month to have enough space to back up my photos, but you can't beat free and unlimited. It took a very long time to upload 15 years worth of photos, but the Google photos service is amazing. This app routinely shows me photos from years and memories past, and helps dig up photos I might have never seen again. The search function only gets better over time and has made it much easier to find the photos I’m looking for. New features are slowly added that continue to make this an even more powerful service. Can not recommend this highly enough, hard to oversell this product/service.

conversations.title: Sanity-saver
conversations.text:
I take tons of pictures and screenshots throughout the day to help with tasks, as a memory aid, and to take the place of pen and paper. It drove me nuts trying to organize or worse, find a picture after I'd taken it. The facial recognition and search function are a lifesaver. 

We have dogs, and I also take a lot of pictures of other dogs. It would be awesome if somehow Google could identify individual dogs so that I could find our dogs as opposed to the bazillion screenshots of dog memes that I save from the Internet. That's the only improvement I would look for. This app is darn near perfect.

^I wrote that years ago and apparently never sent it. Since then Google has done something so we can ID our dogs! It can even identify individual dog breeds pretty well. Love it.

conversations.title: Lost photos :(
conversations.text: I have an IPhone but had run out of storage through my ICloud back in March- Long story short- my phone reset itself back to March and because of my iCloud being full, any pics or contacts added or apps downloaded were lost. I wasn’t too worried because I had the extra back-up for my pics here- for some reason, none of my pics taken after Aug 1st were saved to the google photos app. I lost 2 weeks worth of pictures into cyber space :’( In all the years I’ve had my google acct, I’ve never had any issues and absolutely love the suggested videos and editing suggestions, etc. even though I’m absolutely devastated about losing my pics from the past 2 weeks~ I would still recommend this app and will continue to use & love it.

conversations.title: Simply Amazing!
conversations.text: Google photos is simply amazing.  Not only does it quickly and safely store all of my photos, the Assistant function is awesome.  Face recognition allows me to instantly view every photo of any individual that I ever took a photo of.  The search function is equally great.  For instance type in the word 'dog' and you immediately access every photo you ever took that has a dog in it.  The movie function also enables you to create your own movies or edit the ones Google creates for you.  Google certainly hit a home run with this app.  I have over 35,000 photos stored and use this app daily.  I just took 1200 photos at Disneyworld and organized them in albums for easy viewing and sharing.  Again, simply amazing!

conversations.title: Just Great!
conversations.text: So Google got me to use it over iPhoto because of several reasons.  One, they were first to the punch on "search pictures by content", which works great! Two, because they offer free storage (albeit at a compressed quality) and having my first kid meant lots of pictures are going to be taken. Third, and most importantly, the ease of "aggregation" of all my pictures from different sources. This is a dream once you have it all setup up. I also love the shared albums you can create, which have worked out well as I have one album shared to my entire family with all the pics of my son.  Now everyone always has access to pics of my son. And, now that they have added the ability to share your ENTIRE library with someone else (my wife of course) it is perfect for what I needed. Highly recommended for families.

conversations.title: I hate your update!
conversations.text:
It is cluttered and no longer functional for me ! You changed the entire lay out ! No separation between months with highlights of the month above - now it's just a little bar when you are scrolling.  I absolutely hate it ! I have no use for this any longer. I will be canceling my google storage account - and finding another app that is user friendly and one that I can actually find my photos . This update is garbage ! I don't remember exact dates of photos saved - I spend half a day searching for a particular photo ?! I'm not paying for something I can't use ! Major mistake! The design is terrible! It is a total and complete cluster @&$*ing mess ! Good bye to all the monthly memories that were above each month ! Perhaps we may have wanted to have kept those ! Im so  mad ! After years and years of saving photos - I can't find anything ! I don't like it at all and it seems I'm not alone in this ! I'm angry ! I'm completely devastated it's not organized anymore- it's just a non stop scroll of pictures with no real context or dates - it's like a run on instagram ! I have one of those already! I can not believe I pay you for this mess?! Please return it the previous version ! 
You taken away something that made it feel personal and it was a pleasurable journey to go back k thru the months of each year - now it's a freaking nightmare as it's just a run on mess of cluttered photos ! Awful ! So disappointing! I have stopped  back up and I'm cancelling my  subscription. This is NOT what I pay for . As I stated -I already have an Instagram account !!
Edit to your response: oh yeah I'm sure contacting you there is going to fix everything! Not ! Google you have become a joke ! I'm returning to paying APPLE for additional storage - at least I control my iCloud storage and it's extremely user friendly and I can actually find what I'm looking for because it's organized ! Google Photos is now like a thrift store of random junk - cluttered ,  messy and for the most and  unusable!  This is what AI gets us ! Junk ! 🤬

conversations.title: Lifesaver
conversations.text: I downloaded google photos in the first place so I know that if I ever lose my iPhone, I could always recover the photos online. Today, I was careless and forgot my iPhone passcode. This required me to restart and ultimately resulted in me losing thousands of photos. Thankfully, when I re-downloaded the google photos app, I was relieved to see that all my photos and videos were safe. Although none of the photos or videos in the hidden folder were saved so I lost those for good. Ultimately, google photos is great for reassuring yourself that all of your photos and videos are safe and I highly recommend for anyone who takes hundreds of photos or videos and does not have enough space to save them all.

conversations.title: Couldn't get Along without Google Photos
conversations.text:
I love having Google Photos app on my phone. I back up all my photos very often & delete all the photos from my phone. I like being able to then work with my photos on my laptop on Google Photos. The sync has worked instantly for me. I like that Google Photos organizes some of my photos into albums, and then I make other albums on my own, to share with family members. Great feature. 
Maybe I just haven't found the correct setting yet, but I would like it if Google Photos would just automatically take the photos from my phone whenever I am connected to wifi. So I give it 4 out of 5 stars, with the only issue being ease of use for a 50-something who tries hard to
Keep up on the technology.

conversations.title: Great app to organize your photos ( free)
conversations.text: This a useful app! While they reduce the size of your pictures a bit, they are still good in quality for print for a free service. You can make albums, share them, and even collaborate with others to add pictures from different devices! Google makes it easier and easier to find events, places and people in an increasing mega library of digital pictures you can't possibly keep in your phone unless you back them up somewhere else that will be either inconvenient or will cost you some money on a subscription. There is room for improvement: a smoother switch from different accounts, where photos from profesional personal accounts don’t mix (right now, I find it impossible!)

conversations.title: Google Photos app makes me cry
conversations.text: I want to thank the developers of this app for the intuitive features that take photos based on face recognition to create surprise mini movies for me, complete with accompanying music.  I open the app to find these surprises on a regular basis and can’t help but be filled with happy tears for all the beautiful memories!  The stylized photos are also another great feature of the app.  My photos are available from any platform, whenever I need them, which is the best, and I’ve never encountered any app issues.    I’ve went from the surprise (many years ago) of finding David Hasselhoff inserted into photos, to the joy of a special Mother’s Day movie, a few weeks ago; don’t hesitate to make this your go-to photo app!  Thanks Google!❤️

conversations.title: Best free image tool I use
conversations.text:
I honestly can say this is the best free image tool I use. I bought a Pixel 2 for many of its features, Google Photos was not one of them. I use this with my Pixel 2, Droid Turbo 2, iPad, iPod Touch and now my computer.

The ability to make animations, and the sharing are amazing, but what I truly love is the ability to tag people and pets. It is so easy to be sitting with a friend and simply click their face and be able to share all the photos I have with that person in them. I even use it when talking to my doctor because I copied many of my X-ray pictures and I can pull them up quicker then the doctors system just by searching for ‘ XRay ‘ even if I never tagged the image in any way. The search feature is simply magic.

Thank you! Thank you!

conversations.title: Needs some tweaks.
conversations.text:
I find Google photos app to be very good. I love the auto back up feature. I have mine set so that it will only back up my photos when my phone is on Wi-Fi to conserve my cellular data.

One feature that I find lacking is the ability to do some more complex photo manipulation tasks. Google photos does let you do basic photo manipulation cropping and such. They've been buying a lot of companies that have made photo processing applications. What I have read in the trade magazines is that they were going to incorporate these apps into Google photos. And that is not been done.  I am not asking for a complete  Photoshop app within Google Photos. However, it would certainly be nice to have something beyond the most basic of photo manipulation tasks with in the Google photos application instead of having to go in and out of various other apps.

conversations.title: THE BEST PHOTO APP
conversations.text: I absolutely love Google Photos. It highlights different photos for me to look at and asks if I’d like to order prints. The prints are so affordable and delivered to me. This helps me to accomplish what I keep telling myself to do but keep procrastinating on. The app automatically downloads any photo I take on my phone and safely keeps it. It also suggests photos that can be safely deleted, either because they are screenshots or blurred photos. And Google Photos alerts me when my phone needs more space. It tells me the number of photos that have been safely backed up to Google’s cloud and asks if I’d like to delete these photos from my phone to free up space. Obviously I can’t say enough good things about this app.

conversations.title: The new AI search feature is garbage
conversations.text:
How the original Google photos search feature worked before they incorporated their terrible Gemini ai into the app was perfect. I could search for anything and find my photos with ease. 
Today I was getting a haircut, I'm trying to find a picture from the last time my hair was cut so I could provide my barber a reference, the Gemini ai after I simply searched "hair cut" gave me photos from my camera roll from five years ago at the top of the search, followed by any photo ever that has hair in it?! 
This was not an issue before, I used to he able to just search for haircut, scroll down a little bit and spot my reference photo with ease. 
The Gemini feature in the app is not new, it's been about half a year from what I remember, but they did remove the option to opt out of the ai and use the original search feature, however that is now missing, and the search functionality is useless.

conversations.title: amazing, truly incredible !!
conversations.text:
i've been struggling with my phone's storage for a long time now because i'm such a nostalgic person and i refuse to delete old photos and videos; believing that one day i'd like to look back and reminisce, or i keep them just in case i ever needed them again in the future.

of course, that resulted in lots and lots of storage being taken up by them, up to 60GB. my phone ran out of storage very soon, so i went to my friends to ask for help. one of them owns a google pixel phone and recommended i use google photos.

they convinced me it'd be worth it because the photos'll never disappear, as they're connected to my already existing gmail account. they also said once google photos is done backing up any photos/videos, it offers to delete them off your phone so that you don't have to go and do that yourself.

i trusted my friend with that and gave it a try, and i couldn't have been more grateful for google. thank you so so much for this app. it has freed so much space for me and i still have full access to my precious photos and videos <3

it's really worth more than 5 stars

conversations.title: Works well, but needs improvement
conversations.text: I love this app, but Google needs some improvements. You can search based on the NAME of the photo. I will name a photo so that if I need to find it, I can. Well, found out that it WON’T work. You can search by file name! Crazy. Duplicate photos are a huge issue. No way to deal with that on a sensible basis. Searching by address would be nice, since you have the location. Seems like you can only search by area, and that’s not specific enough to find needed results. I still miss a lot of features the old Picassa had, which google took over then shut down. Why remove all those great features? However searching by name or face works pretty amazingly. Searching by a description works better than expected. Overall I love this app, but please bring back old features and improve on existing ones. Listen to your clients!

conversations.title: Almost perfect.
conversations.text:
This app does feel a little limited on what you can do related to backing up photos and videos. I haven’t found any option to skip a photo/video you don’t want to back up unless you delete it. Another small problem is that when you back up all of your gallery to Google Photos the app itself will be the amount of GB all of your gallery is. And if you don’t delete it it’s the same thing as having your gallery duplicated. ALSO the auto back up feature is kind of broken when trying to back up couple hundred photos, it will stop even if you have background refresh turned on. I had to sleep with my phone unlocked doing the backup because I was unsure it would work with it turned off. Great app overall just has some small issues that bothers me.
-Iphone 6s

conversations.title: It's been the best for so long, it's getting hard to compete with itself
conversations.text:
Sadly I've grown bored with Google Photos. I wish it did more. 

Storage
Already being a Google One subscriber, it says there's nothing I can do to upgrade as I near capacity. Wish there was some kind of built-in review to capture inadvertent excess and prompt you with an action like download and delete or deep storage transfer to Drive or Dropbox. There's also no way to see where the top offenders for size are including large and/or long videos, exorbitantly large raw image formats, etc. 

Backend storage options
Honestly doesn't make sense that there wouldn't be a backend for storage hand-off. Still keeps people connected and using the software. Just allows easier transition to alternative storage. I would rather be holding my own roll of film.

Shared album limitations
I've also gotten feedback from friends about not being able to filter a shared album, if for example we share a single Google photos album and we all contribute, how do I see only the ones that I took exclusively, or ones for 2 but not there other 6.

Search
But of course I do admit that I love the object and people recognition searches. Beyond the storage, that's what I'm here for.

conversations.title: Google Account Storage Problems
conversations.text:
READ THIS IF YOU HAVE STORAGE PROBLEMS!!!

I downloaded Google Photos and allowed access to all my photos. I could no longer use my Gmail due to a full storage. I was afraid that if I deleted the Google Photos app that my camera roll would delete. I ended up changing Google Photos permissions in settings to not allow access to my camera roll. Then I deleted the app. I went to the Google Photos webpage on my computer and deleted all of the photos stored there. After that my Google Account gained its storage back because I am able to send and receive emails, however I am still seeing a notification that my storage is full. When I look at my storage it says that it actually isn’t full. Regardless, my camera roll retained all of its photos and I can now send and receive emails. I believe that whole process was not designed or explained well. I could not find any help or suggestions from Google.

iPhone user: In fact google photo at first makes it look like a great idea, it’s seamless to synchronize your photos from iPhone to the app.

conversations.title: Getting worse
conversations.text:
What have they done to search and the organisation of photos? Half of my date searches now return zero results unless I use very specific (unintuitive) date formats. Photos repeat when scrolling search results, and the results aren’t as relevant as they were in the past. If I make a copy of an old photo, it’s usually lost forever in my library as it appears to be time-stamped the same as the original - shouldn’t be.
I’m not sure if these changes were made to improve the performance and cost optimisation on Google’s side, but the user experience has significantly deteriorated.
Once a great product.

conversations.title: Trust Google to be so fantastic!!
conversations.text: This app was recommended to me by an IT (Apple) trainer on a cruise I was on a few years ago. Whilst my 30,000 family photos stored on my Mac are took some time to upload - a couple of weeks actually! (but thankfully all for free!!), this app is a brilliant mobile device compliment to the Google photos software which gives me complete remote access to ALL of my photos and videos, something which, if done through Apple Photos, would now be costing me a monthly subscription. Just hope Google never start to charge!! This is an incredible bit of software and cannot be recommended highly enough. The reminders of events from years ago on anniversaries are great and I love the videos google throws together, sometimes within a few hours of upload - also love how you can have any number of devices (cameras, macs, PCs, phones etc) all subscribing to the same account so that the whole family's photos can be accessed by any family member either via the app or by logging into the google account ( tip - set up a specific family gmail address for this that you can all access and subscribe to - save having to give out your passwords for your personal google account). Being able to share your library with people who do not subscribe to the photo collection is also a neat touch. Why would you not use this app?!! The search capability is also incredible via the really Clever mechanucs behibd the system. Just search “dog” and see all your photos containing a dog!! More great enhancements to come over time, I'm sure!

conversations.title: Brilliant until the new announcement
conversations.text: I’ve been using Google Photos for a few years now, mainly as my primary backup of my photographs taken using my phone. It allows me to keep my phone space free while being able to formulate albums, mark favourites and easily share memories to other apps. I am an avid photographer of my children (my memory isn’t as good as it was, thanks baby brain) and the Recent Highlights/highlights of this week from previous years has enabled me to easily revisit cherished moments. Now if I had written this review last week, it would have been 5 stars, but the announcement that there will now be a charge has put a dampener on whether I continue to use this app or find another free way of storing my photographs. I’m trying to find a way of writing this without sounding petty (and failing) but it’s disappointing to see this currently free service now be charged for additional storage, of which shall be within 7 months if the calculated projected timescale for me is correct. The fact that it was free for unlimited storage at a marginally lower quality (which was still amazing quality) was a huge pull for me to use this service. I don’t have a lot of spare time to sit and manually back up and organise my photos so this app has really helped me to feel organised and up to date when I’ve been able to have a spare few minutes. I am really reluctant to have my photos in different places, but if the charges come through then that may have to be the case.
